UN MESSAGE EN FRANÇAIS SUIVRA. Good day, Thank you for contacting Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) We have received your enquiry concerning your Confirmation of Permanent Residence document that has expired or will soon expire. We are currently making additional verifications in order to respond to your request.

The Government of Canada is closely monitoring the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) and any impacts on IRCC clients. All our efforts are dedicated to answering your concerns as the situation evolves. However, it may take some time before a response is sent to you. In an effort to reduce duplicate requests, please refrain from sending your enquiry multiple times. Rest assured that we will communicate with you as soon as we have more information. In the meantime, we invite you to visit our website regularly to obtain the most up-to-date information. We thank you for your patience in this difficult time. Sincerely, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada [https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html) Note The information provided may change without notice. If there is conflicting information between the text in the email and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, the Citizenship Act or their regulations, the Act and/or Regulations prevail. This email was sent to you in the language of your choice. The information on the IRCC website is available in both official languages. The masculine form may have been

# Bonjour,

Merci d'avoir contacté Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC). Nous avons reçu votre demande concernant votre document de confirmation de résidence permanente

# qui a expiré ou expirera bientôt. Nous effectuons présentement des vérifications supplémentaires afin de

répondre à votre requête. Le gouvernement du Canada surveille étroitement le nouveau coronavirus (COVID-19) et toute incidence sur les clients d'IRCC. Tous nos efforts sont consacrés à répondre à vos préoccupations au fur et à mesure que la situation évolue. Cependant, cela pourrait prendre un certain temps avant qu’une réponse vous soit envoyée. Dans l’effort de réduire les requêtes en double, veuillez éviter de nous envoyer votre requête à plusieurs reprises. Soyez assuré que nous communiquerons avec vous dès que nous aurons plus d’information. Entre-temps, nous vous invitons à visiter notre site Web régulièrement afin d'obtenir des renseignements à jour. Nous vous remercions de votre patience durant cette période difficile.

# Bonjour,

## Merci d'avoir communiqué avec Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada.

Nous vous remercions de votre patience et de votre compréhension concernant le délai de réponse à votre requête en raison de la situation actuelle liée à la COVID-19.

Notre système indique que vous avez contacté le Centre de soutien à la clientèle par téléphone après avoir envoyé cette requête par courriel et nous sommes heureux de voir que vous avez eu la chance d'obtenir une réponse à votre requête. Si vous avez des questions en suspens à la suite de cette conversation téléphonique, nous vous invitons à nous écrire en utilisant le formulaire Web d'IRCC.

Nous vous invitons à consulter la page Les répercussions de la maladie à coronavirus (COVID-19) sur l’immigration, les réfugiés. la citoyenneté et les services de passeport régulièrement pour obtenir les dernières mises à jour.

Nous vous remercions de votre patience durant cette période difficile.

De plus, veuillez noter que deux méthodes s'offrent à vous pour vérifier l'état de votre demande en ligne. Vous pouvez vérifier l’état de votre demande :

Soumise par la poste (si elle n’a pas été liée à un compte en ligne) : 0en utilisant notre outil en ligne État de la demande du client (EDC), qui est mis à jour quotidiennement.

- Soumise en ligne ou soumise par la poste et liée à un compte en ligne : o par l’entremise de votre compte en ligne.
Nous espérons que l’information fournie aide à répondre à votre demande.

# Good day,

Thank you for contacting Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

### Coronavirus-Approved PRs

We verified the information you provided. The Government of Canada is closely monitoring the new coronavirus (COVID-19) and its impact on IRCC clients.

If you are outside Canada: On March 20, 2020, the Government of Canada provided updates on exemptions to travel restrictions in place to stop the spread of the coronavirus and protect the health and safety of Canadians. If you were approved for permanent residence before the travel restrictions were announced on March 16, 2020, but have not landed yet, you will be able to come to Canada. The travel restriction exemptions that were announced are now in place. If you're exempt, you can now travel to Canada. If you're travelling by air, you need to pass a health check before you're allowed to board your flight. Anyone who shows symptoms of COVID-19 will not be allowed to enter Canada by air. When you arrive in Canada we'll assess your health before you leave the port of entry. You must isolate for 14 days even if you have no symptoms. This is mandatory. Only people who provide essential services and truck drivers who regularly cross the border to maintain

## the flow of goods are exempt from the isolation requirements.

We invite you to consult the How COVID-19 is affecting business at IRCC page to answer your most common questions about travel restrictions and exemptions. If you are inside Canada:

We understand that these measures will affect several IRCC clients, including those who have received a Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) and are currently inside Canada. Validating a COPR at a Port of Entry (POE)

Due to the current travel restrictions, you should not travel to a POE to validate your COPR. Travelling to a POE from inside Canada for the purpose of getting immigration services is not considered essential travel, and you will not receive these services.

### Appointment at a local IRCC office

- All in-person permanent resident landing appointments at the local IRCC offices have been cancelled.
000051

Immigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'nformation divulguée en vertu de la toi sur l’accès à Finformalion

We are looking into alternative means to provide permanent resident landing services, including possibly by telephone. You will be contacted directly to reschedule your appointment. Local offices are reduced to critical services, therefore, no appointments can be scheduled at this

## time. What happens next?

•Maintaining a legal temporary resident status is an important requirement. If your status is about to expire, you must apply online for an extension (visitor, student or worker). We invite you to visit our website regularly to receive up-to-date information as more announcements are made.

Please be assured that we continue to closely monitor the situation closely and will provide you with the most current information as the situation evolves.

Sincerely,

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada [https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html)

# Bonjour,

Merci d'avoir communiqué avec Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC).

### Coronavirus-RP approuvés

Nous avons vérifié l’information que vous avez fournie. Le gouvernement du Canada surveille étroitement le nouveau coronavirus (COVID-19) et toute incidence sur les clients dIRCC.

Si vous êtes à l'extérieur du Canada :

Le 20 mars 2020, le gouvernement du Canada a fait le point sur les restrictions de voyage en place afin d’arrêter la propagation du coronavirus (COVID-19) et de protéger la santé et la sécurité des Canadiens.

Si votre résidence permanente a été approuvée avant que les restrictions de voyage ne soient annoncées le 16 mars 2020, mais n’avez pas encore fait valider votre confirmation, vous serez en mesure de venir au Canada. Les exemptions annoncées aux restrictions de voyage sont maintenant en place. Si vous êtes exempté, vous pouvez maintenant voyager vers le Canada.

Si vous voyagez par avion, vous devez passer une vérification de votre état de santé avant d'être autorisé à monter à bord de votre vol. Quiconque présente des symptômes de COVID-19 ne sera pas autorisé à prendre l'avion vers le Canada.

000052

Immigration, RefugeesImmigration, Réfugiés and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'nformation divulguée en vertu de la toi sur l’accès à Tinformation

À votre arrivée au Canada, nous vérifierons votre état de santé avant que vous quittiez le point d'entrée. Vous devrez vous isoler pendant 14 jours même si vous ne présentez aucun symptôme. Ceci est obligatoire.

Seuls les personnes qui fournissent des services essentiels et les camionneurs qui traversent régulièrement la frontière pour maintenir le flux de marchandises sont exemptés des exigences d'isolement.

Nous vous invitons à consulter la page Incidences qu'a le COVID-19 sur les activités à IRCC afin de trouver les réponses à vos questions les plus courantes.

Si vous êtes à l'intérieur du Canada :

Nous comprenons que ces mesures auront des incidences sur plusieurs clients d’IRCC, incluant ceux qui ont reçu une confirmation de résidence permanente (CdRP) et qui sont présentement au Canada.

Valider une CdRP à un point d'entrée (PDE)

- Étant donné les restrictions de voyage actuelles, vous ne devriez pas vous rendre à un PDE pour valider votre CdRP. Se déplacer à un PDE depuis le Canada dans le but d’obtenir des services d’immigration n’est pas considéré comme un déplacement essentiel, et vous ne recevrez pas ces services.
## Rendez-vous à un bureau local d'IRCC

Tous les rendez-vous d’octroi de résidence au bureau local d'IRCC ont été annulés. Nous cherchons des moyens de fournir des services aux résidents permanents qui viennent d’arriver, par exemple, par téléphone. Nous communiquerons directement avec vous pour reporter votre rendez-vous. Les bureaux locaux n’offrent que les services critiques, par conséquent, aucun rendez-vous ne peut être fixé à ce moment-ci.

## Qu'arrivera-t-il ensuite?

Conserver son statut légal de résident temporaire au Canada est important. Si votre statut expire bientôt, vous devez présenter une demande de prolongation en ligne (visiteur, étudiant ou travailleur). Nous vous invitons à consulter notre site Web régulièrement. Il sera mis à jour en fonction de l’évolution de la situation.

Soyez assurés que nous continuons de surveiller étroitement la situation et à vous donner l’information la plus récente au fur et à mesure que la situation évolue.

## UN MESSAGE EN FRANÇAIS SUIVRA

# Good day,

Thank you for contacting Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)

In order to help us better serve you, please follow the below guidelines to ensure your query goes to the right department to ensure we respond as quickly as possible:

## Replacement of Document

If your enquiry is regarding replacing a valid temporary resident document (i.e.: Visitor Record, Study Permit, Work Permit, and/or Temporary Resident Permit), a Confirmation of Permanent Residence, or a Record of Landing, please visit the IRCC Website for the concerned form to complete. All instructions can easily be found within the kit, specifically the Instruction Guide IMM

5545.
## Amendment of Document

If your enquiry is regarding correcting an error, therefore requiring an amendment, on a valid temporary resident document (i.e.: Visitor Record, Study Permit, Work Permit, and/or Temporary Resident Permit), a Confirmation of Permanent Residence, or a Record of Landing, please visit the IRCC Website for the concerned form to complete. All instructions can easily be found within the kit, specifically the Instruction Guide IMM 5218.

## Case Status

If your enquiry is regarding a case status which has not yet been answered via other channels, please write back to us using the IRCC Web form and choose one of the following options:

Temporary Residence (applied online) or Temporary Residence (applied by Mail) located in the drop down menu under the heading Enquiry for any temporary residence application (i.e.: Visitor Record, Study Permit, Work Permit, and/or Temporary Resident Permit) Permanent residence (applied by mail) or Permanent residence (applied online) located in the drop down menu under the heading Enquiry for a permanent residence application under an economic stream (i.e.: Provincial Nominee, Skilled Worker, Caregiver, etc.).

We thank you for your understanding and patience as we seek to provide existing and future Canadians with the best client service.

Sincerely,

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada [https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html)

## Remplacement d'un document

Si votre requête concerne le remplacement d’un document de résidence temporaire valide (p.ex. : fiche de visiteur, permis de travail, permis d’études, et/ou permis de séjour temporaire), une confirmation de résidence permanente ou une fiche relative au droit d’établissement, veuillez visiter le site Web d'IRCC afin d'avoir accès aux formulaires à compléter. Toutes les instructions peuvent être trouvées facilement à l’intérieur de la trousse de demande, spécifiquement le Guide IMM 5545.

## Modification d'un document

Si votre requête concerne la correction d'une erreur, nécessitant ainsi la modification d'un document de résidence temporaire valide (p.ex. : fiche de visiteur, permis de travail, permis d’études, et/ou permis de séjour temporaire), une confirmation de résidence permanente ou une

formulaires à compléter. Toutes les instructions peuvent être trouvées facilement à l’intérieur de la trousse de demande, spécifiquement le Guide IMM 5218.

## État de la demande

Si votre requête concerne l’état de votre demande et n’a toujours pas été répondue via d’autres canaux tels que nos agents au téléphone, un représentant rémunéré, un centre communautaire, etc., veuillez nous réécrire en remplissant le formulaire Web d'IRCC et sélectionner l'une des options suivantes :

- Résidence temporaire (appliquée en ligne) ou Résidence temporaire (soumis par la poste) dans le menu déroulant qui se trouve sous la rubrique Demande pour toute demande de résidence temporaire (p.ex. : fiche de visiteur, permis de travail, permis d’études, et/ou permis de séjour temporaire). Bonjour,

Nous avons reçu votre requête concernant le programme de parrainage des parents et grands-parents (PGP).

Veuillez noter que cette boîte de réception est destinée aux personnes qui ne sont pas en mesure de remplir le formulaire en ligne Intérêt pour le parrainage en raison d’une incapacité.

Si vous n’avez pas d’incapacité vous empêchant de remplir le formulaire en ligne Intérêt pour le parrainage :

Vous devez présenter le formulaire Intérêt pour le parrainage PGP en ligne, Le formulaire en ligne sera disponible sur notre site Web entre midi, HAE, le 13 octobre et midi, HNE, le 3 novembre 2020.

Si vous ne pouvez pas remplir le formulaire en ligne en raison d’une incapacité :

Vous avez jusqu'à midi, HNE, le 3 novembre 2020 pour demander le formulaire dans un autre format (une demande par personne). La date limite pour soumettre le formulaire Intérêt pour le parrainage dans un autre format vous sera communiquée lorsqu’il vous sera envoyé. Pour demander ce formulaire dans un autre format, nous vous invitons à réécrire à IRCC.PGP.CORRECTION-CORRECTION.PGP.IRCC@cic.gc.ca ou appelez-nous au 1-888-242- 2100 (à partir du Canada seulement). Vous devrez inclure tous les renseignements suivants : ovotre nom complet (le répondant potentiel), o votre numéro de téléphone, o le type de format requis (papier, grande police de caractères ou braille), 0comment souhaitez-vous recevoir le formulaire d'Intérêt pour le parrainage (par la poste ou par courriel), o adresse postale, si vous voulez recevoir le formulaire par la poste, 0adresse de courriel, si vous voulez recevoir le formulaire par courriel, Oconfirmation que vous demandez le formulaire dans un autre format en raison d’une incapacité.

## Veuillez noter que :

Le formulaire en ligne Intérêt pour le parrainage respecte les normes du gouvernement du Canada en matière d'accessibilité du Web. Le formulaire Intérêt pour le parrainage permet aux répondants potentiels d'informer IRCC qu'ils aimeraient parrainer leurs parents ou grands-parents. Le formulaire Intérêt pour le parrainage n’est pas un formulaire de demande. Soumettre le formulaire plus d'une fois n'augmentera pas vos chances d'être invité à présenter une demande. Nous supprimerons toutes les entrées en double et ne conserverons que votre dernière soumission.

Thank you for contacting Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

The Government of Canada is closely monitoring the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) and any impacts on IRCC clients. We are contacting you to follow up on the email regarding your permanent residency application.

To manage the outbreak of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19), the Prime Minister announced travel restrictions that will limit travel to Canada. We understand that these measures will affect several IRCC clients, including those who have received a Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) and are currently inside Canada.

- Validating a COPR at a Port of Entry (POE): due to the current travel restrictions, you should not travel to a POE to validate
your COPR, 。travelling to a POE from inside Canada for the purpose of getting immigration services is not considered essential travel, and you will not receive these services.

- Appointment at a local IRCC office:
all in-person permanent resident landing appointments at the local IRCC offices have been cancelled until further notice, local offices are reduced to critical services, therefore, no appointments can be scheduled at this time.

- What happens next? 0maintaining a legal temporary resident status is an important requirement. If your
status is about to expire, you must apply online for an extension (visitor, student or worker), 0we invite you to visit our website regularly to receive up-to-date information as more announcements are made Please be assured that we continue to closely monitor the situation and provide you with the most current information as the situation evolves.

To obtain the latest information on the situation, we invite you to consult the How the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) is affecting immigration, refugees, citizenship and passport services page.

# Good day,

Thank you for contacting Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

We determined that your request did not relate to the type of enquiry selected in the IRCC Webform

## (Replacement documents, Amendment to documents and Verification of Status Documents). We invite

you to consult the scenarios below and resubmit your enquiry with the correct type of enquiry so that the responsible department replies to your request as soon as possible.

#### Replacement of Document

If your enquiry is regarding replacing a valid temporary resident document (i.e.: Visitor Record, Study Permit, Work Permit, and/or Temporary Resident Permit), a Confirmation of Permanent Residence, or a Record of Landing, please visit the IRCC Website for the concerned form to

### complete. All instructions can easily be found within the kit, specifically the Instruction Guide IMM

5545.
#### Amendment of Document

If your enquiry is regarding correcting an error, therefore requiring an amendment, on a valid temporary resident document (i.e.: Visitor Record, Study Permit, Work Permit, and/or Temporary Resident Permit), a Confirmation of Permanent Residence, or a Record of Landing, please visit the IRCC Website for the concerned form to complete. All instructions can easily be found within the kit, specifically the Instruction Guide IMM 5218.

Providing an additional document or enquiring about an application case status

If you wish to provide an additional supporting document for your application or are enquiring regarding a case status which has not yet been answered via other channels, please write back to us using the IRCC Web form and choose one of the following options:

Temporary Residence (applied online) or Temporary Residence (applied by Mail) located in the drop down menu under the heading Enquiry for any temporary residence application (i.e.: Visitor Record, Study Permit, Work Permit, and/or Temporary Resident Permit). Permanent residence (applied by mail) or Permanent residence (applied online) located in the drop down menu under the heading Enquiry for a permanent residence application under an economic stream (i.e.: Provincial Nominee, Skilled Worker, Caregiver, etc.).

We thank you for your understanding and patience as we seek to provide existing and future Canadians with the best client service.

## Sincerely,

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada [https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html)

# Bonjour,

Merci d'avoir communiqué avec Immigration, Réfugiés et Citoyenneté Canada (IRCC).

Nous avons déterminé que votre requête n’est pas reliée au sujet choisi dans le formulaire Web d'IRCC (Remplacement de documents, modification de documents et vérification du statut). Cependant, nous vous invitons à consulter les différents scénarios ci-dessous et à nous réécrire en choisissant le type de demande présentée approprié pour vous assurer que le département responsable puisse vous répondre le plus rapidement possible.

## Remplacement d'un document

Si votre requête concerne le remplacement d’un document de résidence temporaire valide (p.ex. : fiche de visiteur, permis de travail, permis d’études, et/ou permis de séjour temporaire), une confirmation de résidence permanente ou une fiche relative au droit d’établissement, veuillez visiter le site Web d'IRCC afin d'avoir accès aux formulaires à compléter. Toutes les instructions peuvent être trouvées facilement à l'intérieur de la trousse de demande, spécifiquement le Guide IMM 5545.

## Modification d'un document

Si votre requête concerne la correction d'une erreur, nécessitant ainsi la modification d'un document de résidence temporaire valide (p.ex. : fiche de visiteur, permis de travail, permis d’études, et/ou permis de séjour temporaire), une confirmation de résidence permanente ou une fiche relative au droit d'établissement, veuillez visiter le site Web d'IRCC afin d'avoir accès aux formulaires à compléter. Toutes les instructions peuvent être trouvées facilement à l'intérieur de la trousse de demande, spécifiquement le Guide IMM 5218.

Fournir un document additionnel ou se renseigner à propos de l'état d'une demande

Si vous désirez fournir un document additionnel à votre demande ou si votre requête concerne l’état de votre demande et n’a toujours pas été répondue via d’autres canaux tels que nos agents au téléphone, un représentant rémunéré, un centre communautaire, etc., veuillez nous réécrire en remplissant le formulaire Web d’IRCC et sélectionner l’une des options suivantes :

Résidence temporaire (appliquée en ligne) ou Résidence temporaire (soumis par la poste) dans le menu déroulant qui se trouve sous la rubrique Demande pour toute demande de résidence temporaire (p.ex. : fiche de visiteur, permis de travail, permis d’études, et/ou permis de séjour temporaire). Résidence permanente (appliquée en ligne) ou Résidence permanente (soumis par la poste) dans le menu déroulant qui se trouve sous la rubrique Demande pour une demande de résidence permanente sous l’une des catégories du volet économique (p.ex. : candidats des provinces, travailleurs qualifiés, aides familiaux, etc.).

Nous vous remercions pour votre compréhension et votre patience alors que nous nous efforçons d'offrir le meilleur service à la clientèle aux futurs et actuels Canadiens.

Sincèrement,

## 26 Inadmissibility 517 No 2020-12-03 1

Some people are not allowed to come to Canada. They are known as inadmissible under Canada's immigration law. There are several reasons for inadmissibility.

### Common offences

Among all reasons for inadmissibility, criminality is the most common.

Here are examples of common criminal offences that would result in a refusal of entry in Canada or extension of your stay:

Driving under the influence (of alcohol and/or narcotics), Driving while intoxicated,

## Operating a vehicle while intoxicated,

Breaking and entering,

## Theft, petty theft, petty larceny, shoplifting, robbery,

armed robbery, Possession of stolen goods, Possession of a controlled drug or substance, Trafficking a substance, and Fraud, forgery, counterfeiting.

#### How to overcome inadmissibility

If you have committed a crime or you have been convicted of a crime, you could nonetheless obtain the authorization to enter Canada depending on:

The type of crime, How long ago the crime took place, and How you have behaved since.

There are four possibilities to overcome inadmissibility:

Deemed rehabilitation,

### Rehabilitation,

Record suspension, or Temporary resident permit.

We invite you to consult our website for more information on each of the possibilities. 27 Confirmation of departure519No 2020-12-03 1

### If the Government of Canada has told you to leave

the country, meaning that you are the subject of a removal order, you have 30 days to see an officer at a port of entry* to confirm your departure. The officer at the port of entry will:

## Verify your documents,

Fill out a Certificate of Departure (IMM 0056), and

Ask you to sign this certificate as proof that you have left Canada.

A deportation order can be issued in the following cases:

You do not confirm your departure from Canada with an officer, or

You do not get a certificate of departure within 30 days after the removal order was issued.

## 28 How to appeal as a sponsor522No 2020-12-03 1

As a sponsor, you can appeal the decision of a Canadian visa office to refuse to issue permanent resident visas for the persons* you sponsored.

Your appeal must be filed with the Immigration Appeal Division (IAD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB).

### For more information, please consult:

the IRB website, the Operational Manual OP 21, and contact the IAD.

If you did not receive the Notice of Appeal:

please contact the visa office to request a copy.

If you do not want to appeal:

please follow the instructions for the refund of the Right of Permanent Residence Fee included in the information package you will receive from the visa office.

*The Family Class includes your spouse, common- law partner, conjugal partner, dependent children, adopted children or children to be adopted in Canada, parents, grandparents, orphaned relatives under the age of 18, and one other relative related by blood or adoption (if you meet the requirements). 29 Judicial review 523No 2020-12-03 1

will depend on the type of application. In certain cases, it is possible to file an appeal, for example when the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) has rejected your claim for refugee status.

When an appeal is not possible or when the appeal was refused, a judicial review may be requested with the Federal Court of Canada. The judicial review is done in two steps: first is the authorization and then the actual request for judicial review. In the case of decisions made by the iRB, a request for review by the Federal Court automatically puts a removal order on hold, and you can stay in Canada until the Court makes its decision.

Differences between an appeal and a judicial review

An appeal and a judicial review are very different. The following table explains the differences.

## Appeal

#### Judicial Review

### An appeal is filed with the Immigration and Refugee

## Board (IRB).

A judicial review is filed with the Federal Court of Canada.

An appeal can be filed only for certain types of applications.

### A judicial review can be filed following any type of

decision taken by the department as well as following appeal decisions taken by the IRB.

An appeal decision is based on the content or substance of the application (i.e., on the documents or the facts presented).

A judicial review decision is based on how the initial officer came to a decision.

An appeal decision can overturn the initial decision.

000143

# Identifier Content Identifier Draft CreateCreateUpdate (Prefornatted Date User Date Text)

A judicial review decision does not overturn the initial decision. It orders to re-do the initial decision- making process. This does not mean the original decision will necessarily be reversed.

Principal reasons to request a judicial review:

The decision maker has committed an error in law, obvious or not, The decision maker has not understood the facts or seems to have ignored a fundamentally important fact, The decision maker has violated a principle of natural justice or has not respected the principle of procedural equity, or The decision taken by the decision maker oversteps the boundaries of the powers conferred to him by the IRPA and the application of its regulations.

Although you may represent yourself at the Federal Court, we recommend that you retain a lawyer because the procedures are complex.

Time frames for filing a judicial review

## The decision is made in Canada

The application must be commenced within 15 days after the date on which the person concerned is notified of or otherwise becomes aware of the matter.

The decision is made outside of Canada

The application must be commenced within 60 days after the date on which the person concerned is notified of or otherwise becomes aware of the matter.

You will find more information on the Federal Court 000144

You do not have the right to appeal a negative decision on your application to sponsor a member of the *Family Class in the following cases:

The person you were sponsoring is a member of the Spouse or Common-law Partner in Canada Class. The person you were sponsoring was refused on

## grounds of security, violating human or international

rights, serious criminality or organized criminality. The person you were sponsoring was refused on grounds of misrepresentation,

this does not apply if the person you were sponsoring is your spouse, common-law partner or child.

The principal applicant was not refused,

e.g., you wanted to sponsor your father, but the application was refused because his new wife, who was supposed to come to Canada with him, committed serious crimes and she is not allowed to come to Canada. *The Family Class includes your spouse, common-law partner, conjugal partner, dependent children, adopted children or children to be adopted in Canada, parents, grandparents, orphaned relatives under the age of 18, and one other relative related by blood or adoption (if you meet the requirements).
### 31 Pre-removal risk assessment 526 No 2020-12-03 1

If you are under a removal order (i.e., if you are told that you must leave Canada), in most cases, you will be given the opportunity to apply for a Pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA). That is to determine whether or not your life would be in danger if you had to return to your country.

For more information, please visit our website.

## 32 Repayment of cost of removal528No 2020-12-03 1

A person who has been removed from Canada at the expense of the Canadian Government and who wants to come back will have to repay the cost of removal before an Authorization to Return to Canada can be given.

For more information, please visit our website. Stay of removal No 2020-12-03 1

## 34Authorization to return to Canada531No 2020-12-03 1

If you have been the subject of a removal order from Canada, you will probably need an Authorization to Return to Canada (ARC) if you want to come back.

There are three types of removal orders:

Please consult our website to determine if you need an ARC to return to Canada.

### Applying for an ARC

If you are applying to come to Canada for any reason (visiting, studying, working or immigrating,

## including family class sponsorships), you should not submit a separate application for an ARC. If

your application is approved, the ARC will be dealt within the context of that application.

However, if you are not submitting an application to come to Canada (e.g., you are visa or eTA exempt) and you believe that you need an ARC, you should contact a Canadian visa office before coming to Canada. This type of application is not available online.

Every country decides whom it considers to be a citizen. If more than one country recognizes you as a citizen, you have dual citizenship. Canadian citizens are allowed to take foreign citizenship while keeping their Canadian citizenship.

If you are a permanent resident, but not a Canadian citizen, please ask the embassy of your country of citizenship about its rules before applying for Canadian citizenship. If you are granted Čanadian citizenship, you will have dual citizenship.

### Travelling as a dual citizen

If you are in Canada for a short period of time, it is possible that you had to get a Temporary resident visa (TRV) to enter the country. It is a sticker added to a page in your passport.

When you arrived in Canada, an officer provided you with information regarding the length of your stay. Generally, you are allowed to stay in Canada as a visitor for *six months without having to ask for an extension of your stay. An officer can give you a longer or shorter amount of time.

The expiry date on your TRV indicates by which date you can enter Canada and the expiry date of your authorized stay indicates by which date your stay ends.

*For example, if you entered Canada on January 5th, 2017, you must leave by July 5th, 2017, at the latest.

visa (TRV)

You have a TRV and would like to know if you can leave Canada and come back?

### Single-Entry TRV

If you have a single-entry TRV, you will generally need a new visa to come back to Canada. You can ask to come back to Canada on your original single-entry TRV, if you will:

only visit the United States* or St. Pierre and Miquelon, and return to Canada before the end of your approved stay in Canada.

### Multiple-Entry TRV

You can ask to come back to Canada if you have a multiple-entry TRV and it has not expired.

### Expired TRV

You can ask to come back to Canada on your original TRV, even if it is expired, if you will:

only visit the United States or St. Pierre and Miquelon, and return to Canada before the end of your approved stay in Canada.

# Labour Market Impact Assessment Exemption -2020-12-03 1

Academics

Generally, if you want to apply for a work permit, you need a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) from Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) and a job offer letter from your future employer.

As an exception, you can apply for a work permit without a LMIA if you are an academic, such as:

A guest lecturer invited by a post-secondary institution to give a series of lectures for a period of less than one academic term or semester,

An elementary or secondary school teacher coming to Canada under an exchange agreement between a foreign educational institution and a Canadian provincial government or school board, or

A visiting professor working for two academic years or less at a post-secondary institution while keeping the job he has outside Canada Labour Market Impact Assessment Exemption -2020-12-03 1 Athlete, coach and trainer

Assessment

## 132What is work?1094 No 2020-12-03 1

See if what you are planning to do while in Canada* is considered work.

### Work is an activity:

For which income or commission is earned, or

## That competes directly with Canadian citizens or permanent residents' activities in the Canadian

labour market.

An activity that competes directly is:

An activity that a Canadian or permanent resident should have an opportunity to do, or A business activity that competes in the marketplace.

In other words, an activity which does not take away opportunities for Canadian citizens or permanent residents to obtain employment or experience in the workplace is not considered work.

If you are engaged in an activity for which you are being paid, it is considered work.

#### Being paid includes:

Money paid by an employer to an employee, Money received to perform a service or an activity, and Receiving a commission.

## If needed, further information on this subject is

available on our website.

*A person teleworking for a Canadian company while residing outside of Canada is not considered to be working in Canada. No work permit is needed for them while they reside physically outside of Canada. 133 Information for employers 1096 No 2020-12-03 1

## 136Who is a family member1121 No 2020-12-03 1

#### A family member is:

A spouse or common-law partner who is 18 years old or over, A dependent child, or The dependent child of a dependent child.

## 137Who is a Co-signer1122 No 2020-12-03 1

A co-signer can be your spouse or common-law partner* who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Canada and who is 18 years of age or older. They may help you meet the income requirement by co-signing your sponsorship application.

#### The co-signer is asked to:

Meet the same eligibility requirements as you (i.e. the sponsor), Agree to co-sign the undertaking form (IMM 1344A), and Agree to provide financial support to the sponsored person and his family members, if applicable, for their basic needs during the length of time covered

### by the undertaking.

Only a spouse or common-law partner can co-sign a sponsorship application.

It is not necessary to have a co-signer when:

You don't have to meet the financial requirements, depending on the type of application, or The sponsor meets the income test.

*A common-law partner is a person with whom you have lived continuously for at least one year before signing the undertaking.

## 143Proof of cohabitation1139No 2020-12-03 1

When you apply to sponsor a common-law partner, you are asked to prove that you have been living with your partner for at least 12 consecutive months in a relationship similar to a marriage.

While cohabitation means living together continuously, from time to time, one or the other partner may have left the home for work or business travel, family obligations, and so on. To qualify as continuous, the separation must have been temporary and for a short term. Separate periods of cohabitation adding up to one year cannot be considered.

Here is a list of items that can be used as proof of cohabitation:

Joint bank accounts and/or credit cards, Joint ownership of residential property, Joint residential leases, Joint rental receipts, Joint utility bills (electricity, gas, telephone), Proof of shared management of household expenses, Shared responsibility for household management, household chores, Evidence of joint purchases (especially for household items), Mail addressed to either or both of you at the same address, Important documents for both of you showing the same address, (e.g., identification document, driver's license, insurance policy, etc.),

For applications received before October 24, 2017, and

## 149 Obligations of a sponsor1147No 2020-12-03 1

When you sponsor someone, or co-sign a sponsorship application, you sign a contract named undertaking, promising to give financial support for

### the basic needs of the people you are sponsoring,

and their *family members.

What are the basic needs?

Food, clothing, shelter and other basic things for everyday living, Dental care, eye care and other health needs not covered by public health services.

By signing an undertaking, you are also accepting to repay the government any social assistance payments (i.e. welfare) made to the sponsored

person and their family members, if applicable, during the time covered by the undertaking. These amounts need to be repaid to the government

### before you can sponsor someone else, or co-sign

another sponsorship application.

#### Important reminder

A change in situation (such as separation, divorce, grant of Canadian citizenship for the applicant, unemployment, financial status, etc.) does not cancel the undertaking, the responsibility to provide for the basic requirements of the sponsored person and his family members, if applicable, continues for the entire length of the undertaking.

#### How long is my undertaking?

This period begins on the day permanent resident status is granted and lasts until the end of the validity of undertaking.

The duration of the undertaking varies, based on the type of family member you are sponsoring, and is between 3 and 20 years for non-residents of Quebec. The province of Quebec imposes its own undertaking length.

### *A family member is a spouse, common-law partner,

dependent child or dependent child of a dependent child. 150Sponsors in Quebec (Family Class)1148 No 2020-12-03 1

Reuniting family members is as important to us as it is to you.

When you live in Quebec, the provincial government, through the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI), is responsible for determining whether or not sponsors have the financial ability to sponsor members of the family class* and also the length of their undertaking.

The process with the MIFI begins after the federal

### government, through Immigration, Refugees and

Citizenship Canada (IRCC), has completed a review of your sponsorship application. Our department will then confirm you can apply for a Certificat de sélection du Québec (CSQ) with the MIFI.

How to prepare your request

If the federal eligibility requirements are met, the Case Processing Centre (CPC) will send the sponsor a letter with instructions to:

Download the MIFI undertaking kit to complete, and Submit it to the MIFI with a copy of the letter from

### CPC.

*If you cannot get a police certificate, we invite you to include a written explanation with your application and an original letter from the police authorities confirming that they will not issue a certificate. 152Residency obligations for permanent residents 1154 No 2020-12-03 1 In order to maintain your permanent resident status,

you are required to be physically present in Canada for at least 730 days (which is equal to two years) within a five-year period. Those days of physical presence do not need to be continuous.

If you have been a permanent resident for less than five years, you must show that you will be able to

# Text)

meet the residency obligation within five years of the date you became a permanent resident.

Calculation

The residency obligation may be verified either when meeting an immigration officer (for example when entering Canada) or when submitting an application for a permanent resident card.

To calculate residency, the officer will use the current date (if you are in person with the officer) or the signature date on your PR card application and go back 5 years. If within that period, you were physically present in Canada for 730 days or more, you meet the residency obligation. For the purpose

## of this calculation, any part of a day spent in

Canada is counted as one full day.

Exceptions

Some exceptions to the physical presence may apply. For example, in the following situations, days

## spent outside Canada may also count towards the

730 days if:

## You are travelling with your spouse or partner who

is a Canadian citizen;

You are a child travelling with his or her father or mother who is a Canadian citizen;

You are an employee of (or under contract to) a Canadian business.

We invite you to consult the Appendix A: Residency obligation of the permanent resident card application kit for more information on how to calculate the possible exceptions and what happens if you are unable to meet the minimum requirements. Loss of Permanent Resident Status No

## 153 1157

To keep your permanent resident (PR) status, you must have been in Canada for at least 730 days during the last five years. You can lose your PR status if:

An officer determines that the residency obligation was not respected,

## You voluntarily renounce your PR status,

A removal order comes into force after an admissibility enquiry or hearing (e.g., misrepresentation or serious criminality), or

Refugee claim inside Canada 2020-12-03 1

Canada is a participant in many international agreements and examines all applications for protection made inside Canada.

A person can ask for protection from Canada:

### When they enter Canada through:

an airport, a land border, a seaport, or

After their entry to Canada, at an IRCC office.

If you are in Canada with or without legal status, and you fear to return to your home country, you can claim the refugee status by following these steps:

Present yourself at the closest IRCC office providing

#### What happens next?

The officer you make your refugee claim to will:

Determine if your claim is eligible to be referred to the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada

### (IRB),

Ġive you instructions about the next steps.

## 272Refugees selected outside Canada 1386No 2020-12-03 1

The Canadian government helps refugees resettle in Canada through the Refugee and Humanitarian Resettlement Program, which includes:

Convention refugee abroad class, and Country of asylum class.

The term resettlement is used by IRCC to describe

### the legal process of bringing a refugee to Canada to

live as a permanent resident. To be eligible for resettlement to Canada, the person must be outside of Canada and outside of their home country or country where they normally live, and they must meet the definition of a refugee under Canada's Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

Many organizations help in the resettlement process by identifying and referring refugees when there is no other solution or effective protection available. These organizations include the:

United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), Private sponsorship groups, and Other designated referral organizations.

A person cannot apply directly for resettlement to Canada and cannot make a claim at an Embassy of

### Canada.

For more information on how Canada's refugee system works and to find out if you are eligible, we invite you to visit our website.

## 276 Work Permit-Applying Outside Canada 1412No 2020-12-03 1

A work permit is usually required to work in Canada on a temporary basis. If your intention prior to come to Canada is to work in our labour market, then it is important to apply for this document before your arrival to Canada.

#### How to apply

### To apply, please visit our website.

#### Helpful tips

The Instruction Guide and the Document Checklist will provide you with all the information necessary to help you submit a complete application. Depending on your intended occupation and length of employment in Canada, you may be requested to undergo a medical examination. Have your documents ready, as you may be asked to attend an interview or send further information.

Please visit our processing times page to find out

### how long it may take to process your application.

## 277 Study Permit-Applying Outside Canada 1414 No 2020-12-03 1

### document before entering the country.

#### How to apply

#### To apply, please visit our website.

#### Helpful tips

The Instruction Guide and the Document Checklist

### will provide you with all the information necessary

to submit a complete application. Depending on your length of study in Canada, you

### may be requested to undergo a medical

examination. Have your documents ready, as you may be asked to attend an interview or send further information during the processing of your application.

## 278Application for citizenship-Adoptions on or after 1417 No 2020-12-03 1

January 1, 1947

To support you on the last phase of the adoption process, the following kit is for people who were or will be adopted by a Čanadian citizen, and who are applying for a direct grant of citizenship.

### More precisely, the category of adopted persons

includes:

Adopted persons who are minors (under 18 years of age) at the time of application, Persons who were adopted as minors but are adults

### (18 years of age or older) at the time of application,

and Persons who were or will be adopted as adults.

Details on eligibility can be found on our website.

This is a two part application process

### When you are ready to present an application for

Canadian Citizenship-adopted person:

Please send the Part 1: Confirmation of Canadian citizenship of the adoptive parent(s) to the Case Processing Centre in Sydney, Nova Scotia first:

this part is to confirm that at least one adoptive parent is a Canadian citizen at the time of the adoption.

Once Part 1 is approved, you will receive a letter indicating to:

### fill out Part 2: Adoptee's application, this part is to

confirm that the adoption meets the requirements, and

### send it to the address provided on that letter.

### 343 Proof of financial support-Study permit 1637 No 2020-12-03 1

What is a proof of financial support?

It is a document that proves you have enough money to pay for your needs, and those of your family members during your stay in Canada, and for your return home.

#### Here are a few examples:

If money has been transferred to Canada, proof of a Canadian bank account in your name. Proof of a student or education loan from a financial institution. Your bank statements for the past four months. Bank draft. Proof of payment of tuition and accommodation fees. If you have a scholarship or are in a Canadian- funded educational program, proof of funding paid from within Canada. Pay stubs. Letter from your employer stating your salary. Notice of Assessment from the Canada Revenue Agency. Letter of financial support from family members or friends in Canada and proof of their income. Photocopy of a valid return ticket such as a plane, bus or train ticket. Low skill pilot project No 2020-12-03 1

If there is a shortage of Canadian citizens and permanent resident workers somewhere in Canada,

## Employment and Social Development Canada may

issue à Labour Market Impact Assessment, under the Pilot Project for Occupations Requiring Lower Levels of Formal Training, to allow temporary foreign workers to apply for a work permit for a

lower-skilled occupation.

In Canada, lower-skilled occupation is defined as an occupation that usually requires at most a high school diploma or a maximum of 2 years of job-specific training according to the National Occupation Classification (NOC) system. They are coded at the NOC C or D skill level. 345 Special Category-Information Technology Workers 1640

To fill critical shortages in Canada's software industry, Canada had a simplified entry process for workers whose skills were in high demand in that industry.

Under this process, no confirmation letter from

## Employment and Social Development Canada

(ESDC) was necessary for specific jobs in the software industry when hiring a foreign worker, since it did not have a negative impact on Canadian or permanent-resident job seekers and workers.

Please note that the National Confirmation for Information Technology (IT) workers procedure ended on September 30, 2010.

Effective October 1, 2010, employers who wish to hire IT foreign workers are required to apply for a Labour Market Impact Assessment.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada wants to protect the rights of foreign workers when they come to work in Canada by ensuring that employers respect the terms of their offers of employment.

In a work permit application, the employers will be evaluated on:

Rigorous criteria to ensure the job offer is genuine, Compliance to the commitments outlined in job offers to foreign workers hired in the past 6 years, and Compliance with Federal-Provincial/Territorial agreements.

In cases where the employers are found to have not complied with previous commitments to foreign workers, they can be deemed ineligible to hire a foreign worker. The ban duration depends on when the violation occurred. 390 Review of working conditions-Information for1906 No 2020-12-03 1 Workers

430 permanent residence of the person being sponsored is unavailable through our e-Client Application Status (e-CAS) online service. That is the case because that part of the application is not in process yet.

The processing of the application is done in two steps, and there are different processing times for each step.

### Sponsorship application process in two steps:

### Step 1: Sponsor eligibility

At the Case Processing Centre (CPC), an officer will verify if the sponsor is eligible. If the file is transferred to the local office for further verifications, the processing time may differ from the one listed on our website. The acknowledgement letter will be sent once this step is completed.

If the sponsor resides in Quebec, a letter will be sent to them asking to fill out some forms and to send them to the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI)

### Step 2: Final decision

The CPC will send the file to the responsible office. At the office, an officer will verify if the sponsored person meets all the requirements to become a permanent resident of Canada. The processing time for this step varies depending on the case.

Entry and stay in Canada are two different things and the validity of each is determined by different documents.

### Entry-Visa (TRV)

A TRV allows entry into Canada. It is valid for a limited period of time. You must therefore come to

## Canada and present yourself at a port of entry up

until the expiry date on your TRV.

Please note that a valid TRV does not guarantee entry into Canada. If your situation has changed between the date you applied for your TRV and the date you arrived in Canada, an officer will decide if you still meet the requirements to enter the country.

### Stay-Stamp or Status Document

Once entered, the duration of your stay will not be

Re-entry

While you are in Canada, your TRV may expire. This has no effect on the validity and duration of your stay. However, if you plan on leaving and returning to Ċanada, you are required to obtain a new TRV. As an exception, you do not have to obtain a new TRV if you are returning to Canada after travelling only to the United States* and/or St.Pierre and Miquelon by the end of the period initially authorized for your stay or any extension to it.

### of a provincial nominee

An open work permit (open WP) is a great opportunity to work in Canada temporarily. It enables you to work with any employer you wish.

You can apply for an open work permit if you are the spouse/common-law partner of a Provincial Nominee.

#### How to apply

Please visit our website to apply for your:

Initial work permit, or to Extend or change the conditions on your work permit.

We recommend reading the instruction guide, it will help you submit a complete application.

You will need to submit a complete application before your status expires so that your current status is maintained under the same conditions until a decision is made on your permit request (implied status).

Once your work permit is approved, you can start working.

To find out how long it may take to process your application, please visit the processing times page.

In an effort to improve processing times, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada does completeness checks upon reception for all Permanent Resident card (PR card) applications submitted by mail.

When an application is incomplete, the Case Processing Centre (CPC) returns it to the client and includes a letter indicating what is missing. It

## includes 2 options:

Resubmit the application with the missing information and documents,

if you choose this option, please note that it is not necessary to re-sign or re-date the application, as long as it is not dated more than 90 days before we receive it (stale dated), or

Request a refund of the fees because the client no longer wishes to send the application.

For urgent PR card applications that are incomplete, the CPC will not return the application if the client is travelling within 30 days or less. Instead, they will contact them for the missing information and documents. Once the missing information is received by the CPC, if it is complete, they will match that information to the pending application and continue with the processing. However, if there is still missing information or documents, the entire application will be returned with a letter of explanation. Incomplete citizenship proof and grant applications 2455 No 476

Fraudulent websites are attempting to mislead members of the public into thinking that they are official websites of IRCC. They may attempt to charge you for services (such as forms and guides) that are otherwise free on the IRCC website or through the official websites of the Canadian missions and visa offices abroad. They may also try to charge you for services that you may never receive. You should be aware that sending any personal or biographical information to impostor or non-official websites could result in identity theft or the production and circulation of fraudulent documentation.

In order to help you determine if you are dealing with a case of fraud, please consider the following guidelines:

IRCC has only one official website. You will find on this site the guidelines and accompanying forms to assist you in presenting an application under Canada's Immigration Program (they can be downloaded at no cost). Canadian missions and visa offices located outside of Canada operate websites that provide region-specific information on immigration matters. All email addresses, as well as website addresses of Canadian missions overseas and Canadian government departments contain “gc.ca”. Also note that Canadian visa offices and departments do not use commercial email addresses or commercial websites. All forms and guides required to submit an application are available at no cost on the IRCC website. The Government of Canada treats everyone equally, whether or not they use the services of a representative. If you choose to hire a representative, your application will not be given special attention, nor can you expect faster processing or a more favorable outcome.

IRCC recognizes that the use of a representative who charges a fee for conducting business on your behalf is a personal choice. IRCC will only deal with authorized representatives who are members in good standing of a Canadian provincial or territorial law society, the Immigration Consultants of Canada

## Regulatory Council (IČCRC), or the Chambre des

notaires du Québec.

More information on various pieces of identity and immigration documents are available in Appendix 2 (Sample Documents and Stamps) of the Ġuide for Transporters of the Canada Border Services Agency.

# (Preformatted Date User Date Text)

#### Normally, TRV applications are processed by:

A Canadian Visa Office, or The Case Processing Centre (CPC) in Ottawa, Ontario, if you have been legally admitted in Canada as a student or worker.

If your TRV application was submitted by mail to the

### CPC in Vegreville OR Edmonton, Alberta, your

application should be returned to you. We invite you to resubmit it online or by mail to the CPC in Ottawa for processing. 494 If you plan on leaving Canada and returning during2514 No 2020-12-03 1 the validity period of your current status and you require a temporary resident visa (TRV) to re-enter Canada, we invite you to:

### Apply online or by mail,

if you apply by mail, we recommend reading the instruction guide first. It will provide you all necessary information to complete and send your application,

### if you are currently in Canada as a visitor, you must

send your application to a Visa application centre

### (VAC),

if you are currently in Canada and have a valid work permit or a valid study permit, you must send your application to the Case Processing Centre in Ottawa, Ontario.

### You can apply for:

A single-entry TRV, which will allow you to enter Canada only once during the validity of the visa, or A multiple-entry TRV, which will allow you to seek entry into Canada from any country as often as necessary during the validity of the visa.

As an exception, you do not have to apply for a TRV if you are returning to Canada after travelling only to the United States* and/or St. Pierre and Miquelon by the end of the period initially authorized for your stay or any extension to it.

*Including its Territories and Possessions, but not cruises entering international waters.

## 525 Open work permit-Spouse or common-law partner 2851 No 2020-12-03 1

of a post-graduate student holding a work permit under NOĆ O, A or B

An open work permit (open WP) is a great opportunity to work in Canada temporarily. It enables you to work with any employer you wish to work for.

You can apply for an open work permit if you are the spouse/common-law partner of a post-graduate student who already holds a work permit as a highly skilled worker.

### Eligibility to apply

The principal worker needs to be already employed in an occupation under the National Occupational Classification (NOC) skill levels 0, A or B.

To submit the application, here are additional documents you will need to include:

A copy of your spouse/common-law partner's open work permit, A proof that they are employed in an occupation in

## skill level 0, A or B,

A letter from their current employer confirming employment or a copy of their employment offer or contract, and A copy of their last three pay slips.

#### How to apply

Please visit our website to apply for your:

Initial work permit, or to Extend or change the conditions on your work permit.

We recommend reading the instruction guide, it will help you submit a complete application.

Once your work permit is approved, you can start working.

Effective February 4, 2012, IRCC is issuing a new Confirmation of Permanent Residence document (IMM 5688) to certain Permanent Resident applicants. The new document will be printed on a legal size plain paper, rather that the IMM 5292 form. This applies to cases processed within Canada, as well as those processed through the visa offices.

The features of the new IMM 5688 form are the following:

The document is printed on two pages: a IRCC Copy and a Client Copy; The client's photo will be on the IRCC Copy (photo specifications do not change); and The document will not include a shaded signature box. This is no longer required as Permanent Resident cards issued after February 4, 2012 will not display the client signature.

The Client Copy does not require a photo of the holder. Once Permanent Resident status has been granted at the port of entry or the local IRCC office, the Client Copy will be issued to the client as an historical record. New permanent residents will continue to receive their Permanent Resident card (PR card) through the mail within six to eight weeks of being granted PR status and after the Canadian address is provided to IRCC.

## 530Post-graduation work permit validity-Passport will 2973 No 2020-12-03 1

soon expire

As a general rule, immigration documents are issued according to the validity period of the applicant's passport. This means that the validity period of a work permit cannot exceed the passport expiry date.

The post-graduation work permit validity depends on the length of your program of studies and can be valid for a minimum of eight months and up to three years.

If your post-graduation work permit expires before the validity you would have been entitled for, it is possible to ask for an extension of your work permit once your passport will be renewed.

To extend the validity of your work permit:

You can apply by mail and include an explanation letter, the appropriate fees and a copy of your newly extended passport,

we recommend reading the instruction guide first, it will assist you to fill out the form and it will give you the address where to mail it.

## 546 Medical examination for dependent child living 3069No 2020-12-03 1

outside Canada

Applicants who have sole custody of a dependent child living outside of Canada must ensure the child undergoes a medical examination. The Case Processing Centre will send the visa office the information required for the dependent child to be examined.

Dependent children in the sole custody of an ex spouse or ex common-law partner do not have to submit to a medical examination. However, children who are not examined cannot be sponsored as members of the family class at a later time, despite any future changes in the custody arrangements.

### In this case, the applicant should:

Sign and return a statutory declaration acknowledging the above consequences,

or

Inform the CPC that they want the child examined in order to preserve future sponsorship privileges.

The CPC or the IRCC office may insist on a child

Canada and the United States (U.S.) have signed the Safe Third Country Agreement, which stipulates that refugee claimants are required to request refugee protection in the first safe country they arrive in, unless they qualify for an exception to the Agreement.

The Safe Third Country Agreement applies only to refugee claimants who are seeking entry to Canada from the U.S:

At a Canada-U.S. land border crossings, By train, or At airports, only if the person seeking refugee protection in Canada has been refused refugee status in the U.S. and is in transit through Canada after being deported from the U.S. land border crossings.

### The Agreement does not apply to:

American citizens, or Habitual residents of the U.S. who are not citizens of any country (“stateless persons”).

### Important information

The Government of Canada is currently reviewing the Federal Court decision that was released on July 22, 2020, to determine its impacts. Although the Federal Court has made its ruling, that decision does not come into effect until January 22,

## 581 Maintaining a legal status during the process of a 3278 No 2020-12-03 1

permanent residence application inside Canada

When you are in Canada, maintaining a legal temporary status is an important requirement. This is also applicable while your permanent residence application is being reviewed, for yourself and every family member already with you in Canada.

The entry stamp in your passport or your temporary resident document (work permit, study permit, visitor record or temporary resident permit (TRP)) will indicate until what date you can remain in Canada. If your status is about to expire, you can ask for an extension. You may need to extend your status more than once during the process of your permanent residence application.

Every year, the Government of Canada helps thousands of refugees. The purpose of the Joint Assistance Sponsorship (JAS) program is the resettlement of refugees. It is a joined effort between IRCC, who gives financial assistance to the protected person, and a private group, who gives moral support and additional assistance to the protected person.

Within the JAS, sponsorship agreement holders and

## their constituent groups can sponsor refugees with

special needs:

### women at risk,

elderly refugees, persons who have big families, persons with medical disabilities, or victims of trauma resulting from violence or torture.

Since the province of Quebec has its own process to sponsor refugees, we invite sponsors residing in Quebec to contact the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de I'Intégration (MIFI).

A Dependent child can be the child of:

### The sponsor,

The sponsor's spouse or of the common-law partner*, The principal applicant (person being sponsored), or A dependent child of a dependent child.

Note: This also includes children for whom you have

joint or sole custody even if the children usually live with the other parent and will not join you in Canada.

### To be considered a dependent child, the child must

be:

Under 22 years of age and do not have a spouse or common-law partner,

or

22 years of age or older, have depended on their parents for financial support since before the age of

### 22 and be unable to support themselves financially

due to a physical or mental condition.

With the exception of age, dependents must meet these requirements on the day a complete application is received until a final decision is made.

### Please note, a child's age is usually "locked in” when

a complete application is received.

The definition of a dependent child was modified on October 24, 2017. For more information about these changes, please visit our website.

## 655 What is an electronic signature? 3565 No 2020-12-03 1

An electronic signature is required at the end of the online application process in order to create a secure internet environment. This security feature was implemented according to the Privacy Act, to ensure a person's identity and personal information are protected.

When you sign electronically, you are declaring that the information provided in the application is true and that the supporting documents provided are genuine. This means that applicants are no longer required to physically sign an application which will have to be electronically validated when submitted online.

If needed, more information is available for you regarding the electronic signature as well as the online application. 656 Processing Times-Economic Class3567 No 2020-12-03 1

Please visit the processing times page on our website to obtain the estimated time it will take to process a permanent residence application in the economic class.

## Useful tips

The processing times are approximate and vary depending on each case. They are based on how long it took to process 80% of cases.

## 701Student wants to stop studying for a semester 3744 No 2020-12-03 1

Studying and working in Canada can be a rewarding experience.

To be eligible to work off campus, you must be registered as a full-time student.

Even if you remain registered as a student at your school, you are not considered a full-time student if you stop studying for a semester. In this case, you cannot work off campus.

Furthermore, if you are no longer actively pursuing your studies, even temporarily, but wish to remain in Canada, you must apply to change conditions or extend your stay in Canada as a visitor. The application is available on our website.

On June 19th, 2017, Bill C-6, an Act to amend the Citizenship Act and make consequential amendments to another Act, came into force. This is the first reform to the Citizenship Act since the C-24 bill that came into effect on June 19, 2014.

Among the changes that have been made to the

## Citizenship Act, applicants are no longer required to

intend to continue to live in Canada once granted citizenship. This provides more flexibility to Canadians who may need to live outside of Canada for work or personal reasons.

For a complete list of changes made to the Citizenship Act and when they take effect, please consult Bill C-6 Receives Royal Assent: Backgrounder.

If you would like to obtain additional information on Bill C-6, we also invite you to consult the News Release: Citizenship Bill Receives Royal Assent. 772 Request for a refugee profile4031No 2020-12-03 1

If you wish to receive information on refugees you could help settle in your community, please see the Request for a refugee profile application available on our website.

Since 1868, the Department has been issuing different types of certificates (e.g., Registration of Birth Abroad certificate, etc.). Over the years, the format of the certificates and the information that appears on them has changed.

## 806How to view the status of an application online4115No 2020-12-03 1

The e-Client Application Status (e-CAS) service allows you to securely access the status of your immigration and citizenship applications online.

Who can use e-CAS?

You may use this service if you have:

Sponsored a member of the family class, Applied for permanent residence from within or outside Canada, Applied for a permanent resident card (except for new permanent residents), Applied for Canadian citizenship. That includes:

### grant of citizenship,

citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship), resumption of Canadian citizenship, or renunciation of Canadian citizenship.

To access e-CAS, you will be asked to enter personal information, such as:

## 821 Missed citizenship test or interview4136No 2020-12-031

If you have missed or you cannot attend the citizenship test or interview, rest assured that we may be able to reschedule you.

To do so, please send the following information to the responsible office within 30 days from the date of your appointment*:

A reasonable explanation, and Proof to support your explanation.

*If you received an invitation to complete the test online, the 30-day period starts from the last day of the 21-day prescribed timeframe indicated in the invitation you received by email.

You can send your explanation either by:

Using the IRCC Web form, or Email/Mail using the email/mailing address indicated on the email/letter you received,

if you did not receive an email/a letter, you may find the mailing address of the office on our website.

Your application may be considered abandoned if:

Once the 30-day period has elapsed, no response has been provided, or An acceptable explanation was not provided.

#### Important facts to keep in mind

If you received a first notice to write the test or for an interview, but did not attend, and

### You did not contact us to let us know or did not

provide an acceptable explanation:

you will be automatically rescheduled at a later date and will receive a final notice,

however, if an acceptable explanation was provided, you will receive a new first notice.

If you are a permanent resident of Canada and you wish to become a Canadian citizen, the first step is to verify if you meet certain conditions.

We invite you to consult the web page Determine your eligibility-Citizenship where you will find the necessary information.

## Citizenship language requirements2020-12-03 1

In order to apply for Canadian citizenship as an adult, one of the requirements is to have an adequate knowledge of one of the official languages of Canada, which are English and French.

This means you should be able to:

Take part in short, everyday conversations about common topics, Understand simple instructions, questions and directions, Use basic grammar, including simple structures and tenses, and Show that you know enough common words and phrases to answer questions and express yourself.

If you are 18 to 54 years of age, it is required that you send documents with your citizenship

### application to prove your language abilities. In order

to verify if you have the necessary documents, we invite you to use the following wizard:

## Acceptable language proof to apply for citizenship

You can also find the type of proof we will accept in the citizenship application guide.

familiarise yourself with all the requirements for Canadian citizenship.

### 879Study permit exempt-All categories4505No 2020-12-03 1

In most cases, obtaining a study permit is necessary if you want to study in Canada.

You may be exempt from obtaining a study permit to go to school in Canada if you are:

Taking a course or program in Canada that lasts six months or less, A family member or staff member of a foreign representative to Canada, A member of a foreign armed force, or A citizen of another country who has Registered Indian status in Canada.

For more details, please visit our website. 880 Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) 4506 No 2020-12-03 1 exemption-Mobilité francophone

Generally, if you want to work in Canada, a LMIA from Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) and a job offer letter from your employer are required to get a work permit.

Under certain regulations, a LMIA is not required if you are a French-speaking or bilingual skilled worker who intends to work in a Francophone community outside Quebec.

#### Important facts to keep in mind

We invite you to use the online tool to verify if you are eligible to apply for a work permit without a LMIA under the Mobilité francophone.

If you apply for a work permit, the steps that your employer needs to take are the following:

Pay the employer compliance fee, and Prepare and submit an offer of employment through

### the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's

Employer Portal.

#### What's next?

Your employer will provide you with the offer of employment number to indicate in your work permit

## 966In order to maintain their permanent resident status, 4784 No 2020-12-03 1

it is required for a permanent resident to be physically present in Canada for at least 730 days (which is equal to two years) within a five-year period. Those days of physical presence do not need to be continuous.

If permanent residency was granted less than five years ago, then it is necessary to show that the residency obligation will be met within five years after becoming a permanent resident.

Calculation

The residency obligation may be verified either when meeting an immigration officer (for example when entering Canada) or when submitting an application for a permanent resident (PR) card.

To calculate residency, the officer will use the current date (if the PR is in person with the officer) or the signature date on their PR card application and go back 5 years. If within that period, they were physically present in Canada for 730 days or more, they meet the residency obligation. For the purpose of this calculation, any part of a day spent in

000561

### Draft

## Identifier Content Identifier

# (Preformatted Text)

Canada is counted as one full day.

Exceptions

Some exceptions to the physical presence may

### apply. For example, in the following situations, days

spent outside Canada may also count towards the 730 days if:

They are travelling with their spouse or partner who is a Canadian citizen; They are a child travelling with his or her father or mother who is a Canadian citizen; They are an employee of (or under contract to) a Canadian business. The Appendix A: Residency obligation of the PR card application kit provides more information on how to calculate the possible exceptions and what happens if a permanent resident is unable to meet the minimum requirements. We invite the applicant to visit our website to find out how to apply for:

An initial study permit, or To extend your study permit.

We recommend reading the instruction guide, it will help them submit a complete application.

If the applicant has renewed their passport since entering Canada, they will have to submit a photocopy of the:

new passport, and stamp placed in their old passport.
