by Employment and Social Development Canada (ÉSDC) determines the impact of hiring a foreign worker on the Canadian labour market. A positive LMIA indicates that there is a need for a foreign worker to fill the job and that no Canadians are available to do the job.

#### The factors considered by ESDC include:

Could a citizen or permanent resident of Canada fill the job? Will the hiring of a foreign worker help create

### opportunities or benefits for Canadian job seekers?

Are the working conditions and pay offered similar to what a citizen or permanent resident of Canada would expect to receive?

Please note that in some cases, a LMIA is not needed.

Apply for a LMIA to ESDC, and

## 1039We are pleased to provide you with information4899 No 2020-12-03 1

about the Temporary Resident Visa (TRV).

The TRV is a document required for citizens of certain countries who want to come to Canada for a short period of time as a temporary resident. It is a sticker the size of a passport page.

Upon arrival in Canada, if the applicant meets the requirements and they wish to work, study or visit, they may be issued a work permit, study permit or visitor record at the port of entry.

If an applicant requires a TRV to travel to Canada, here is what they should consider:

It is valid for a limited period of time:

it is important to come to Canada and present themselves at a port of entry before the expiry date on the TRV. if the TRV is not used before the expiry date, it will no longer be valid. the length of stay in Canada as a visitor, worker or student is not related to the TRV's expiry date.

A valid TRV does not guarantee entry into Canada:

at the port of entry, an officer will determine if the applicant still meet the requirements to enter the country.

## Multiple entry visa:

allows the applicant to enter and leave Canada for six months at a time, without having to reapply for a new visa each time. it can be valid for up to 10 years, or one month before the passport expires, whichever is earlier.

If the holder of an expired TRV plans on leaving Canada during the validity period of their current status, and they require a visa to re-enter Canada, generally, they must submit a TRV application to a

### 1055 A Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) is a document 4922 No 2020-12-031

required for citizens of certain countries who want to come to Canada for a short period of time. It is a

## sticker added to a page in the passport. The length

of stay in Canada is not related to the TRV's expiry date.

Upon arriving in Canada, an officer will decide if the visitor meet the requirements to enter the country.

## The officer may give the visitor a shorter or longer

amount of time for their stay for the following reasons:

The visitor's ability to pay for their expenses and those of their family members coming to Canada with them (financial support), The reason for their visit, The amount of time they ask to stay in Canada for, and

### The expiry date of their passport or travel

document,

their stay cannot be longer than the expiry date of their passport or travel document.

or

If the officer added a date under the stamp in the passport, on that handwritten date.

If the visitor did not receive a Visitor Record and there is no stamp or handwritten date in their passport, their stay will end six months after the day they arrived in Canada.

## 1098Processing times-Application to sponsor a spouse 5001 No 2020-12-03 1

or a common-law partner in Canada

We know how important this process is to you and are hoping to finish processing your application as quickly as we can. So that you can understand the process more fully, we would like to give you a look at what will happen and when.

The process of your application is done in two steps:

#### Step 1: Approval in Principle

At the Case Processing Centre (CPC) in Mississauga, Ontario, an officer will first verify if the sponsor is eligible and if the spouse or common-law partner meets the eligibility requirements to apply to become a permanent resident.

If the CPC makes a positive decision on both these points, a letter stating that the application is approved in principle will be sent to you. If the file is transferred to the local office for further verifications, the processing time listed on our website is no longer applicable.

#### Step 2: Final Decision

After receiving the approval in principle letter, medical, security and background checks have to be done for the sponsored person and the family members included in the application, if applicable.

After all the requirements have been met, a final decision is reached and the file is sent to the local office (unless it is already there). The local office will then contact the sponsored person to give them an appointment so they can become a permanent resident of Canada.

You can visit our website:

To see how long it may take to process your application, and/or For more information on what to expect after a sponsorship application is submitted. Application Forms-Sponsorship of parents and 5009 No 2020-12-03 1 grandparents-Visa office instructions

### 1117 Implied status-Temporary resident5050No 2020-12-03 1

As a temporary resident, it is important to apply to extend your stay in Canada, if necessary, before it expires. Following submission of the application, you are considered to have implied status.

If you apply to extend your stay at the latest on the expiry date of your status:

you will be considered in status as a temporary resident until a decision is made on your application.

If you apply for renewal of your work or study permit at the latest on the expiry date of your status, and your permit expires before a decision is made:

you can continue working or studying under the

### same conditions as your existing permit, as long as

you remain in Canada.

Leaving and re-entering Canada while under implied status:

You may be authorized to re-enter Canada:

As a temporary resident, if your application to extend your stay has not yet been approved (if

### applicable, it will be important to wait* until you

receive your new permit before you start to work/ study):

this applies to you if, among other things:

#### you are temporary resident visa (TRV) exempt,

you hold a valid multiple-entry visa, or you have travelled only to the United States (including its Territories and Possessions, but not cruises entering international waters) and/or

### St.Pierre and Miquelon,

#### As a worker or student:

if the officer determines that your application to

### extend your permit was approved while you were

outside Canada, or

When you send an Application for Permanent Residence in Canada-Humanitarian and Compassionate Considerations, the verification process is done in two steps:

#### Step 1: Approval in Principle

#### Step 2: Final Decision

The second step is to see if you meet all the eligibility requirements to obtain the permanent residence. During this stage of the process, background and medical verifications are done for you and your dependent family members, if applicable.

2021.

## submitting your application. 1156 Express Entry: Immigrating as a skilled worker 5115 No 2020-12-03 1

Thank you for your interest in choosing Canada to settle and continue to develop the skills you have already acquired. Canada has a great job market and plenty of opportunities. If you come as a skilled immigrant, you and your family will benefit from our high quality of life.

The Express Entry (EE) is a system which includes an online account, through which IRCC chooses skilled immigrants as permanent residents. It manages applications for permanent residence under the following federal economic immigration programs:

## The Federal Skilled Worker Program,

The Federal Skilled Trades Program, The Canadian Experience Class, and A portion of the Provincial Nominee Program:

provinces (except Quebec) and territories can also recruit candidates from the EE system through their Provincial Nominee Programs to meet local labour market needs.

We invite you to determine if you are eligible to immigrate under one of the above federal immigration programs before you start the EE process.

### Steps for Express Entry:

### Create your Express Entry profile

this is the first step after you have determined your eligibility,

if needed, the video Immigrate to Canada: How to create an Express Entry profile will take you through the steps of completing an EE profile.

Answer a series of questions

once in your profile, you will be asked to provide personal information such as your work experience or education. You will be awarded points based on the entry criteria and the Comprehensive Ranking System

### The EE Pool

after completing all of the above steps, if you meet the entry criteria, you will be placed in a pool of pre- assessed candidates.

### (If applicable) Register with Job Bank

Job Bank is an easy online tool to help match you

## with employers looking for workers with you skills,

registering with Job Bank is not mandatory.

### Invitation to Apply

we will regularly issue invitations to top candidates

## from the pool so they can apply for permanent

residence. These invitations will ask to submit the application within 90 days of receiving the

## invitation. Instructions on how to apply online for

permanent residence will be enclosed.

You can be in an EE pool for one year (the date is available in your account). Your ÉE profile will expire if you are not invited to apply within that time frame. A message will be sent through your profile to advise you once the 12 months are up. Find out what are the next steps if you are not invited to apply.

Important information if you are invited to apply:

You can choose to decline the invitation, in which case your candidacy will be put back in the pool, as long as you still meet the entry criteria and you may be invited to apply again. If you do not apply within 90 days and you have not declined the invitation, your invitation will expire and you will need to create a new EE profile and be accepted again in the pool to be considered in future rounds.

Our website contains a multitude of information such as the frequently asked questions about Express Entry. If, after consulting the information available on our website you have further questions, you may contact us.

## 1157 Improvements to Express Entry 5116 No 2020-12-03 1

The Government made some improvements to Express Entry. They took effect on June 6, 2017.

Please consult the changes that have been made to verify if they may have an effect on you candidacy.

## 1158Express Entry-Proof of funds-Skilled immigrants 5117 No 2020-12-03 1

In order to meet the minimum requirements of certain Express Entry (EE) programs, a proof of funds to support yourself and your family is required. These amounts are updated each year.

In your EE profile, you have indicated the amount of money that you have to settle in Canada. It is important to update this amount in order to make sure that you meet the proof of funds requirement and to avoid the removal of your profile from the EE pool.

Please note that the proof that you have enough funds will be required when submitting your permanent residence application.

For more information, please visit our website.

## 1159Express Entry Profile5118 No 2020-12-03 1

You will find below useful information that we hope will help you understand Express Entry (EE), in order to make your experience as pleasant as possible.

Before creating your EE profile, it is important to know if you qualify under one of the federal economic immigration programs.

The following information is a brief summary that explains how to fill out your profile on our website.

### Before you start your EE profile:

Once you know under which immigration program you want to apply for, there are important things you will need to determine if you are eligible:

Your language test results, Your NOĆ code, title and skill type or level for the job your work experience is in (as well as the job you plan to have in Canada, if they are different), Your Education Credential Assessment (ECA), if you were educated outside Canada, Your passport or travel document (or other national identity document, if you do not have one),

## A copy of your written job offer from an employer in

Canada, if you have one, and

## A copy of your provincial nomination, if you have one.

The next step is to use our online tool, Come to Canada, to see if you meet the criteria to get into the EE pool. It will take you about 15 minutes.

When you get to the end, a personal reference code will show on the screen. Please write it down. You will need it later when you go to build your profile:

It looks like this: JM1234567890. We use it to bring the answers you provided in the tool into your online profile so you do not have to provide the answers again. If you go to the profile builder directly through your account, you will not have one.

Create your online EE profile:

Create an account, if you need to create one, If you have a personal reference code from the Come to Canada tool, enter it when it prompts you to or enter your personal details, work experience, education, etc., Submit your profile online,

if needed, the video Immigrate to Canada: How to create an Express Entry profile will take you through the steps of completing an EE profile.

If your EE profile is eligible, you can register with the Government of Canada's Job Bank to help you find work.

Job Bank for Job Seekers is an easy, online job search tool which will connect you with employers and jobs in Canada based on your skills and experience. It is not mandatory to register.

Important information:

will help understand the work experience required for Express Entry (EE).

One of the eligibility requirements for EE is your skilled work experience.

## The following table gives a brief overview of the

skilled work experience required for each federal economic immigration programs:

#### Federal Skilled Worker Program

#### Have a work experience:

## Of at least one year of continuous full-time or an

equal amount in part-time*,

## At skill type 0, or skill levels A or B of the National

Occupational Classification (NOC),

### In the same type of job as your primary NOC,

Within the last 10 years,

## Paid work (volunteer work, unpaid internships, etc.,

### do not count).

#### Federal Skilled Trades Program

#### Have a work experience:

Of at least two years full-time or an equal amount of part-time hours*, in a skilled trade,

## Within the five years before you apply,

That meets the job requirements for that skilled trade as set out in the National Occupational Classification (NOC), except for needing a certificate of qualification, and Have an offer of full-time employment for a total period of at least one year or a certificate of qualification in that skilled trade issued by a Canadian provincial or territorial authority.

## Canadian Experience Class

Have a skilled work experience in Canada:

000699

Immigration, Refugees and Cizenship Canadaot Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

# Identifier Content Identifier Draft CreateCreateUpdate (Prefornatted Date User Date Text)

Of at least 12 months full-time (30 hours of paid work per week or more), or an equal amount in part-time hours*, In the three years before you apply, Gained while under temporary resident status with authorization to work, According to the Canadian National Occupational Classification (NOC), skilled work experience means:

## managerial jobs (NOC skill level 0),

professional jobs (NOC skill type A), technical jobs and skilled trades (NOC skill type B).

Note: Work experience in Canada is not counted if

you were:

Studying full-time while you were working, Self-employed, or Not legally allowed to work in Canada.

*To qualify for the full-time work experience, or for the equal amount of part-time, here is how it is calculated:

Full-time at 1 job: 30 hours/week for 12 months = 1 year full time (1,560 hours). Equal amount in part-time: 15 hours/week for 24 months = 1 year full time (1,560 hours). Full-time at more than 1 job: 30 hours/week for 12 months at more than 1 job = 1 year full time (1,560 hours).

For part-time work, you can work more or less than 15 hours/week as long as it adds up to 1,560 hours.

Please note that the work experience must be acquired over a period of at least one year, work in excess of 30 hours/37.5 hours per week over a shorter period cannot compensate for any shorter overall period of experience.

For more information on the work experience, we invite you to consult the ministerial instructions respecting the Express Entry system.

## 1161 Express Entry-Invitation to apply 5120 No 2020-12-03 1

You will find below useful information that we hope will help you understand how the invitation to apply

## works for Express Entry (EE).

### Candidates' selection:

IRCC will invite candidates from the EE pool to apply on a regular basis by having a set of instructions that the electronic system uses to invite candidates from the pool.

These instructions will be posted on this website before each round of invitations:

By posting the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of the lowest-ranked candidate invited, and

## By indicating the date of the invitation.

Please note that the website will post this information before any invitations are sent to the selected candidates.

### Invitation to apply:

If you are invited to apply for permanent residence, you will get a message in your account telling you:

Which program you are invited under, and What to do next.

You will have 90 days to fill out your application for permanent residence and submit all supporting

## documents, such as your language test results and

your police certificates.

Please consult the Apply-Skilled immigrants (Express Entry) page to learn more about the process.

### Change in circumstance:

If your circumstance has changed or the

## information in your EE profile is no longer accurate,

we invite you to recalculate your score in the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) available on our website.

Please also visit our website to know more about when a candidate's situation changes after the ITA is issued.

### Helpful tips:

The invitation to apply provides specific instructions to follow. We recommend you follow these instructions within the time frame given. To obtain more details concerning the submission of a complete application, please consult the website.

## If you wish to clarify some information, feel free to

add an explanation letter in your application for permanent residence. if your application for permanent residence is rejected for being incomplete, the fees will be refunded and instructions on how to create a new EE profile will be provided in the letter. 1162 Express entry-Points system (CRS) 5121 No 2020-12-03 1

You will find below useful information that we hope will help you understand how the points system works for Express Entry (EE).

Candidates get points based on a number of criteria, and the highest ranking candidates in the pool are invited to apply to immigrate to Canada.

The Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) is a points-based system that is used to assess and score a candidate's profile to rank them in the Express Entry pool.

The total number of points that may be assigned under the Comprehensive Ranking System is 1200 points.

If you have not filled out an Express Entry profile and you would like to see what your CRS score might be, please use this Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) tool.

### Helpful tips:

You may also consult the summary of maximum points per factor for Express Entry candidates to determine your score result. Please note that if the level of education includes two or more certificates, diplomas, or degrees, one must be for a program of three or more years. To obtain more details concerning Canadian educational credentials, please refer to subsection 30 (1) of the Ministerial Instructions issued for the EE program. You can view your CRS score result in your profile. If you are an active candidate in an EE pool and believe that the current amount of points you have does not reflect your situation, you can update your profile. Please consult our Express Entry rounds of invitations to see the CRS score of lowest-ranked candidate invited to apply for permanent residence. Express Entry-Technical enquiries No 2020-12-03 1

You will find below frequently asked questions about Express Entry (EE).

### Technical enquiries about your account:

Here is some information that you may find useful:

It is possible to update your EE profile if your profile is either:

not submitted yet, or submitted and your profile was found eligible for the pool.

You can also update fields in your EE profile that may be greyed out. If you have just reset your account because you lost your username and/or password and you do not see your application anymore, you can link your application directly from your account.

## If you have already submitted your online

permanent residence application, it is too late to add any supporting documents unless you received a message asking you to upload additional documents. You can view your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score result in your profile. If you are an active candidate in an EE pool and believe that the current amount of points you have does not reflect your situation, you can update your profile. The ministerial instructions concerning the invitation to apply for permanent residence are updated after every round of invitations. You can see the CRS score of the lowest-ranked candidate invited. If your CRS score is equal or higher to the one indicated, you should receive the invitation in the next 24 to 48 hours following the announcement. If you are using a cellular or a tablet, you may not be able to view/read letters in your account. A payment is required only once you submit your application for permanent residence.

### Finding a solution to technical difficulties:

We invite you to consult Express Entry's (EE) frequently asked questions. It contains a multitude of information that may answer your questions. If you are still experiencing technical difficulties:

we invite you to fill out the IRCC Web form and include:

screen shots showing the full browser window, including the website address field of the:

page where you are experiencing problems/trying to 000703

A Job Match account with Job Bank is an easy, online tool to help match you with employers looking for workers with your skills.

in step 3, you will need your Express Entry profile number and your job seeker validation code. 1165 Express Entry-Modifying the personal information 5124 No 2020-12-03 1

the View your profile under the heading Your Express Éntry profile status, On the Express Entry profile page, click on Modify Family Information at the top of the page.

## 1171Facilitation visas5133 No 2020-12-03 1

If you are a Canadian citizen and wish to travel to Canada, but do not have a Canadian passport, we invite you to contact the Consular section of Global Affairs Canada.

However, there are exceptional circumstances where IRCC can facilitate the travel of a dual national by placing a facilitation visa counterfoil into the passport of the Canadian's other nationality.

Here are some examples of circumstances that might warrant the issuance of the visa:

## When new, replacement or emergency passports

cannot be issued in a sufficiently timely fashion and where the travel is urgent:

for Canadians in distress (lost/stolen documents), for dual nationals coming to Canada for the first time, for dual nationals who did not obtain a Canadian passport prior to leaving Canada,

Children born in Canada to foreign nationals, who have returned to their country, and do not wish to «claim» the citizenship automatically granted to Canadian born children, Foreign nationals who are adopted under the Citizenship adoption process, Etc.

If needed, more information is available for you regarding facilitation visas.

## 1230 Bill C-6 5229 No 2020-12-03 1

On June 19th, 2017, Bill C-6, an Act to amend the Citizenship Act and make consequential amendments to another Act, came into force. This is the first reform to the Citizenship Act since the C-24 bill that came into effect on June 19, 2014.

## Through these changes, the Canadian government

is aiming to:

Streamline the citizenship process,

## Enhance program integrity, and

Repeal certain provisions of the Act that treated dual citizens differently than other Canadians.

For a complete list of changes made to the Citizenship Act and when they took effect, please consult Bill C-6 Receives Royal Assent:

## Backgrounder.

If you would like to obtain additional information on Bill C-6, we also invite you to consult the most recent News Release: Government of Canada implements new legislative changes to the Citizenship Act.

As of June 27, 2017, citizens of Antigua and Barbuda will need a temporary resident visa (TRV) to enter Canada.

This means that any existing Electronic Travel Authorizations (eTÀ) issued to citizens of Antigua and Barbuda are no longer valid.

We invite you to visit our website for more information on the steps you'll need to follow, depending on your situation.

## 1233Short-term highly-skilled worker5232 No 2020-12-03 1

Since June 12, 2017, high-skilled workers coming to perform work of a short duration may be exempt from the requirement to obtain a work permit.

The new work permit exemption for highly-skilled workers applies to all NOC 0 and NOC A workers. Eligible workers will be allowed one 15-day work permit-exempt stay in Canada every six months, or one 30-day work permit-exempt stay every 12 months.

If you wish to know more, please consult our website.

## 1234 Short-term researcher 5233 No 2020-12-03 1

Since June 12, 2017, researchers taking part in short-duration research projects being conducted in Canada may be exempt from the requirement to obtain a work permit.

Researchers coming to Canada are permitted one 120-day stay or less every 12 months without requiring a work permit when they are working at a publicly funded, degree-granting institution at the college or university level or at an affiliated research institution.

If you wish to know more, please consult our website.

## 1243 As a visa-exempt foreign national, you only require5246 No 2020-12-03 1

an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) if you enter Canada by air. If you wish to enter by land or sea, an immigration officer at the point of entry will assess whether you meet the requirements to enter Canada as a visitor.

### Requirements to visit Canada

In order to let you enter Canada as a visitor, the immigration officer must be satisfied that your stay will be short-term and that the reasons you are giving for your visit are authentic.

It means that you will have to demonstrate to the officer that you:

Will leave Canada at the end of your authorized stay, Have enough money to pay for travel costs and for your needs while you are in Canada, Will not work or study in Canada without authorization, Do not have a criminal record and are not a security risk to Canada, and Are in good health and, if required, have done a medical examination.

If you are unsure whether you should apply for an eTA or not, we invite you to use our online questionnaire. No 2020-12-03 1

## 1247Port of entry secondary examination5250 No 2020-12-03 1

Thorough port of entry examinations are necessary to ensure the safety of all Canadian citizens, permanent residents and visitors to Canada. Secondary examinations are, for the most part, considered routine and should not be viewed as an accusation of wrongdoing on the part of the traveller.

Nevertheless, if you are required to pass to a secondary examination every time you enter Canada and you would like to know the reason and/ or request a review of your file, we invite you to fill out the Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) Feedback Form. The CBSA team will look into it and provide you with a response. ## 1262Gender identifier “X”5269 No 2020-12-03 1

Since June 4, 2019, individuals are able to request the “X” gender identifier printed on documents issued by IRCC. This includes Canadian passports and travel documents, citizenship certificates and permanent resident cards.

To request a gender identifier “X” on your:

Canadian passport or travel document, please consult:

Choose or update the gender identifier on your passport or travel document

#### Citizenship certificate, please consult:

Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply

Permanent resident card, please consult:

Applying for a Permanent Resident Card (PR Card) -

## First application, replacement, renewal or to change gender identifier

Temporary residents (TR) can be issued a TR document with an “X” gender identifier if the passport issued by their country has an "X" (or an equivalent, non-binary option) in the sex field.

For more information, we invite you to consult the following pages:

Help Centre

### 1269 Application forms-Citizenship grant-Minor5291

applying as an adult under subsection 5(1)

Overview

Bill C-6, An Act to amend the Citizenship Act and to make consequential amendments to another Act, which received Royal Assent on June 19, 2017, now makes it easier for minors to obtain citizenship and its benefits without a Canadian parent due to the removal of the age requirement for a grant of citizenship under subsection 5(1).

The amendment allows a parent or person having custody of the minor, or empowered to act on their behalf by court order, written agreement or operation of law, to apply for citizenship on behalf of the minor, unless that requirement is waived by the Minister.

#### How to apply

Please follow these instructions in order to apply for Canadian citizenship as a minor under subsection 5(1), To ensure you are submitting a complete application, please consult the Instruction guide, Once you are ready to mail your application, please send it to the address in the guide.

### 1343Police certificates-Citizenship5396No 2020-12-03 1

To apply for Canadian citizenship as an adult, you need to meet the residency requirement.

If, within the last 4 years, you spent 183 or more consecutive days, since the age of 18, in a country other than Canada, you need to provide a police certificate. A police certificate is necessary for each country where you spent 183 consecutive days or more.

If you are unable to obtain a police certificate, please include a letter of explanation with your application.

#### A few useful details

#### The police certificate:

#### must have been issued:

after the last time you were in that country, or no more than 6 months before the date you sign your citizenship application, and

## is typically valid for one year from the date it is

issued.

## 1395 The Express Entry (EE) system ranks candidates in 5463 No 2020-12-03 1

the pool using their Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score. The system ranks all candidates based on the information provided in their profile (skills and experience).

If you update the information in your EE profile, the CRS will update your score. If your situation has changed but your profile was not updated by the time the invitations were sent, your new score will not be considered anymore for that round. Please note that it may take up to 24 hours for the system to update your score.

After verifying the information provided, we have noticed that your EE profile was submitted October 24,2017.

For the invitation round of February 7, 2018, the CRS score of lowest-ranked candidate invited was 442. If more than one candidate has the lowest score, the cut-off is based on the date and time the candidate submitted their EE profile. For this round of invitation, the tie-breaking cut-off date was May 29,

2017.

When filling out the Come to Canada eligibility tool, the system will ask you a series of questions to verify if you meet the minimum requirements to submit your application online.

#### What happens if I am eligible?

You will be provided a unique reference number, known as the Personal Reference Code (PRC).

The PRC will generate a personalized, streamlined document checklist that you can follow whether submitting an online or paper application.

When entering the PRC, it is important to do so in the exact format as follows: AB1234567890. You may only use the PRC once.

I am receiving an error message when entering my PRC. What can I do?

You can fill out the Come to Canada eligibility tool to obtain another PRC, or Fill out the questionnaire directly from your online account. To do so:

under the section Start an application, click on Apply to come to Canada, then under the section I do not have a Personal Reference Code, click on the button that corresponds to the type of application you wish to submit.

Every year, approximately 1,000 applicants for permanent and temporary residence in Canada receive a medical inadmissibility finding. It is determined that their health condition may adversely affect health or social services, and this may lead to them being found to be medically inadmissible.

On April 17, 2018, IRCC Minister announced changes to the medical inadmissibility provision of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. These changes will ensure that the immigration policies are better align with Canadian values and reflect the importance that the Government places on the inclusion of persons with disabilities.

For more information, please consult the News release on our website. 1439Required documents for the citizenship interview5510 No 2020-12-03 1

## which has your photograph and signature on it (e.g., driver's license, health card, passport, etc.),

All your original documents that support your citizenship application (e.g., Immigration Record of Landing (IMM 1000) or Confirmation of Permanent Residence (IMM 5292 or IMM 5688), birth certificate, etc.), Your Permanent Resident card, if you have one, and All passports and travel documents in your possession (current and expired).

We strongly encourage you to bring all the required documents with you to avoid being rescheduled.

## 1442 Extend your IEC work permit 5513 No 2020-12-03 1

As a rule, no work permit (WP) extensions are authorized under the International Experience Canada (IEC) Program because its validity period may not exceed the maximum length of stay authorized under the bilateral agreement or arrangement.

Sometimes, a WP may be valid for a shorter time than the validity period allowed because:

Officers cannot issue a WP beyond the validity of the passport, Health insurance validity is shorter than the letter of offer from the employer, The duration of the offer of employment is shorter than the maximum duration allowed, or An administrative error was made.

However, there are instances where Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) may allow IEC clients to increase the validity period of their WP to reach the maximum validity period allowed within a specific category.

### Please consult our website:

To see if you can extend or change your IEC WP, and

## To obtain more details about this program.

## 1456New entry rules for Romanian citizens (June 5th,5536 No 2020-12-03 1 2018)

As of June 5, 2018, Romanian citizens need a valid electronic passport to continue travelling to Canada

without a visa and only require an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) for air travel.

This means that Romanians who hold a non- electronic passport, such as a temporary passport,

need a valid temporary resident visa to travel to Canada.

Please consult the IRCC website to obtain more details.

# 1457Student Direct Stream (SDS)5537No 2020-12-03 1

IRCC is making great strides in promoting Canada as a destination of choice for international students seeking a quality education by finding efficient ways to process applications.

IRCC offers applicants who are legally residing in China, India, Pakistan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Morocco or Senegal faster processing times when applying for a study permit via the Student Direct Stream (SDS).

Applicants from these countries can benefit from the SDS if they can demonstrate upfront that they have the financial resources and language skills to succeed academically in Canada. You can only apply online to be eligible for SDS processing.

To learn more about SDS, we invite you to consult our website. Transition between programs of study – working 5538 No 2020-12-031 off-campus 000850

## 1534 Implications of the Cannabis Act (Bill C-45) 5634 No 2020-12-03 1

On October 17, 2018, Canada has made marijuana (cannabis) legally available to adults under strict new laws. Tough new penalties laws have been imposed on those who:

Drive while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, including cannabis, or Commit cannabis-related crimes.

On December 18, 2018, the impaired driving penalties will take effect. Most impaired driving offences will then be considered serious crimes in Canada.

### How you could be affected

If you commit an impaired driving or a cannabis-related crime, you could face a fine, criminal charges or jail. However, IRCC may also find you inadmissible to Canada for serious criminality. It doesn't matter if the crime happened inside or outside Canada. This means:

Permanent residents may lose their status and have to leave the country, Temporary residents (including visitors, international students and foreign workers) may not be able to enter or stay in Canada, Refugee claimants may not be eligible to have their claim referred for a refugee hearing.

For more information, please consult the following pages:

The notice, How to overcome an inadmissibility,

In an effort to improve processing times, IRCC does completeness checks upon reception for all PR card applications submitted by mail.

The responsible office is currently conducting completeness checks for applications received up to [Date]. Therefore, any application received after this date will not yet appear in our records.

When an application is incomplete, the Case Processing Centre (CPC) returns it to the client and includes a letter indicating what is missing. It includes 2 options:

Resubmit the application with the missing information and documents, or Request a refund of the fees because the client no longer wishes to send the application.

#### Urgent Cases

For urgent PR card applications that are incomplete, the CPC will not return the application if the client is travelling within 30 days or less. Instead, they will contact them for the missing information and documents.

Once the missing information is received by the CPC, if it is complete, they will match that information to the pending application and continue with the processing. However, if there is still missing information or documents, the entire

will the bar and dates.

Permanent residence application

We are happy to inform you that we start accepting permanent residence applications under the Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot (RNIP) Program on November 15, 2019. The goal of this pilot is to help smaller rural and northern communities attract and retain foreign skilled workers to meet their economic development and labour market needs.

#### Who is this pilot program for?

The RNIP is for skilled foreign workers and international students graduates who want to work and live in one of the participating communities. If a community recommends you and you're successful in applying for permanent residence, you'll then move there to work and live.

Please consult our website for information on the eligibility requirements, including how to get a recommendation from one of the communities, to apply for permanent residence.

When the eligibility criteria for the sponsorship are met, the office processing the application will send the sponsor and the person being sponsored the approval in principle letter.

The approval in principle means that you received a letter from the Case Processing Centre or the local office stating that you are eligible to apply for permanent resident status but that a final decision will not be made until all requirements for becoming a permanent resident have been met. These requirements include medical, security and background verifications for you and, if applicable, your family members.

To know how long it may take to process your application, please visit our Web site.

### Helpful tips

In some cases, the approval in principle letter will not be sent at the same time to the sponsor and principal applicant. if the file is transferred to the local office for further verifications, the processing time listed on our website is no longer applicable. If you have not received this letter yet, you may contact the provincial authorities for more details on their eligibility criteria. Please maintain a valid temporary resident status in Canada during the process. While the application is in process, the person being sponsored can apply for a work permit.

## 1612Open work permit for vulnerable workers5753 No 2020-12-03 1

The Government of Canada believes that every worker in Canada is entitled to a safe and healthy work environment where their rights are respected. However, some migrant workers with employer-specific work permits choose to endure mistreatment related to their job rather than report it, fearful of workplace reprisals, as well as

## difficulties in finding a new job and getting a new

work permit.

On May 31, 2019, the IRCC minister announced that starting June 4, 2019, migrant workers who have an employer-specific work permit and are in an abusive situation in relation to their job in Canada will be able to apply for an open work permit.

For more information, we invite you to consult the News release on our website. Pilot project to facilitate sponsorship of previously 5754 No 2020-12-03 1 undeclared/not examined family members

When a person applies for permanence residence in Canada, they are asked to declare all of their family members (spouse, common-law partner, dependent

### children), even if they are not accompanying them in

Canada. In most cases, they also need to be examined. The consequence for failing to declare/ have a non-accompanying family member examined is a lifetime bar on the principal applicant being able to sponsor that family member.

Family reunification is a top priority for the Government of Canada. That is why IRCC put in place a public policy to facilitate the immigration of certain sponsored foreign nationals under the Family Ciass or Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada Class who were not declared/examined previously:

The two-year pilot project will be in effect from September 9, 2019 to September 9, 2021, You may be eligible if:

you’re applying to be sponsored as a spouse, common-law partner, or dependent child under the Family Class or the Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada Class, you were not declared/examined when your sponsor became a permanent resident:

after being sponsored as a spouse, common-law partner, conjugal partner, or dependent child, as a dependent of a resettled refugee/protected person, or after being granted refugee protection in Canada, as a resettled refugee,

AND your permanent residence application:

was still in process on May 31, 2019 (i.e., no final decision made before that date), has been received between May 31, 2019 and September 9, 2021, or is pending reconsideration between May 31, 2019, and September 9, 2021.

## 1616 Super Visa-Co-signer5758 No 2020-12-03 1

When applying for a super visa for parents and grandparents, as the Canadian or permanent resident child or grandchild, you must demonstrate that you have an annual income that is at least equal to the minimum amount of income shown in the Low Income Cut-Off (LICO) table.

If you do not meet the LICO minimum, a co-signer can be added in order to meet the income

The co-signer can be your spouse or common-law partner*.

For more information on the parent and grandparent super visa, please visit our website.

*A common-law partner is a person with whom you have lived in a relationship similar to a marriage for at least 12 consecutive months.

# 1617Invitation to apply-How IRCC calculates the one 5759No 2020-12-03 1

year work experience

When submitting an Express Entry (EE) permanent residence application, you must demonstrate you are meeting the eligibility requirements of one of the federal economic immigration programs. One of the requirements is to enter the month/year of work experience and no specific date. Therefore, you may have received an Invitation to Apply (ITA) even if you are missing a few days of work experience to be eligible.

IRCC officers processing the EE applications are aware of the system calculating months and not actual days/hours worked in a month. When reviewing an application, they will take into consideration factors such as:

Continuous work status,

## The Offer of Employment Letter from the same

employer, and Whether you reach the one year work experience at the time the EE application is submitted/approved or within a few days after.

The decision for approval is at the discretion of the officer. However, the onus is on you to provide all required information and supporting documentation to facilitate the decision.

### 1619 Live-in caregiver-Bridge extension 5766No 2020-12-03 1

A bridge extension is an interim work permit given to a live-in caregiver whose work permit is about to expire, who is between jobs and has not yet found a new employer. When that situation arises, the Case Processing Centre uses a case-by-case approach to assess the file. The extension is usually given for a period of two months.

#### Application form

The application is available on our website. Please:

Indicate your request for a bridge extension (and the reason why) in the Details of Intended Work in Canada section of the application form, Write bridge extension across the top of the form, and Send the application by mail to the Case Processing Centre in Edmonton, AÍberta.

You will need to submit a complete application before your status expires so that your current status is maintained under the same conditions until a decision is made on your permit request (implied status).

The processing fee for the bridge extension is the same as for the work permit.

To find out how long it may take to process your application, please visit the processing times page.

### 1620 Contract 5767 No 2020-12-03 1

Caregivers and their future employers are required to sign a contract that states the conditions and terms of the employment, so that each party understands their rights and responsibilities.

A sample contract is available to give you an idea of the conditions that can be included in the contract.

## 1622 Requirements to become a permanent resident – 5769 No 2020-12-03 1

Home Child-Care Provider Pilot and Home Support Worker Pilot

Launched on June 18, 2019, the Home Child-Care Provider Pilot and Home Support Worker Pilot are two economic pilot programs targeted to foreign national caregivers who:

Have a job offer or Canadian work experience in an eligible caregiver occupation, Meet minimum education and language proficiency requirements.

Caregivers who meet all the requirements but do not have 24 months of Canadian work experience are issued an occupation-restricted open work permit.

### Determine if you are eligible

The Who can apply section indicates if you can apply for permanent residence through these programs if you plan to live outside the province of

## Quebec and you:

## 1625 Extension-Same employer5772No

As a live-in caregiver, if you have been in Canada under the Live-in Caregiver (LCG) program for less than four years and you continue to work for the same employer, you do not need a new Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) from Employment and Social Development Canada when applying to extend your stay in Canada as a worker.

### However, you may need:

A new LMIA, even if you are staying with the same employer, if you have participated in the LCG program for four years, A new WP and a new LMIA if the employer moves and changes province/territory.

If you want to continue working for the same employer, please submit:

A letter from the employer stating that you will continue to be employed on a fuli-time basis for an additional period of time, A copy of a new, or extended, signed employment contract, and For live-in caregivers working in the province of Quebec, a Certificat d’acceptation du Québec (CAQ) from the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI).

## 1626 Procedure for employer 5773No 2020-12-03 1

Hiring a temporary worker as an in-home caregiver is an important decision to make. We want to make sure you have all the information you need at your disposal to guide you through the complete process, from the moment you seek to recruit until the moment the caregiver receives their authorization to work for you.

On the Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDĆ) website, you can learn about the conditions of the In-home caregiver program and you should make sure this program is the best way to meet your needs.

Please note that your caregiver will be able to work for you only when their work permit, showing your name as the employer, is delivered.

## 1627 Re-entry 5774 No 2020-12-03 1

If you want to re-enter Canada as a live-in caregiver after an absence, such as a vacation, it is important to have a:

### Valid work permit,

Valid passport, travel document or identity document, if required, and Temporary resident visa (TRV), if required. To see if you need a TRV to enter Canada, visit our website.

Please note that periods of absence lasting longer than the time allowed by the labour laws in the province you work in (normally two weeks) are not considered periods of employment. Extra vacation time cannot be counted towards the 24 months

## required to apply for permanent residence under the

Live-in Caregiver Program. Also, only periods of work done in Canada count towards the 24 months period requirement.

We cannot guarantee your re-entry to Canada. An

## officer will ask you questions to see if you meet all

of the requirements before allowing you to come back to Canada.

Since we know that becoming a permanent resident is an important event, we want to make sure that you have all the information you need to start this new chapter in your life.

As a permanent resident, you have the right to:

Get most social benefits that Canadian citizens receive, including health care coverage, Live, work or study anywhere in Canada,

## Apply for Canadian citizenship,

Protection under Canadian law and the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

You must pay taxes and respect all Canadian laws at the federal, provincial and municipal levels.

### You are not allowed to:

Vote or run for political office,

## Hold some jobs that need a high-level security

clearance.

For more information, we invite you to consult our website.

### 1649Travel to or stay in Canada with an expired or soon5805 No 2020-12-03 1

to be expired Venezuelan passport

On August 19, 2019, Canada recognized the decree published by the National Assembly of Venezuela on June 7, 2019, to extend the validity of Venezuelan passports for an additional five years past the printed expiry date on the passport (excluding provisional passports).

The total validity of the passport, including the extension, must not exceed 10 years.

Venezuelans who hold a passport covered by the decree may use it to:

Come to Canada or extend their stay as a:

visitor, student, or worker.

## Apply for:

permanent residence, a permanent resident card, or a permanent resident travel document.

Applicants should continue to submit their applications through the normal processes. When necessary, special instructions may be indicated within the applications.

### We invite you to visit our website for more

information.

## 1670 The Resettlement Services Assurance Team 5830 No 2020-12-03 1

The Resettlement Services Assurance Team (RSAT) is responsible for ensuring that, post-arrival, refugees sponsored through the Private Sponsorship of Refugees (PSR) Program are receiving the support that they should be receiving from their sponsorship group, based on program requirements and regulations.

If you believe that your sponsors are not providing you with the support that they are supposed to provide you with, or you are experiencing issues with your sponsors or settlement during your sponsorship period, you should contact the RSAT.

You can reach the RSAT by email: IRCC.PSRCaseReview-RevuedecasPSR.IRCC@cic.gc.ca

For more information concerning the responsibilities of a sponsoring group, please visit our website.

If your sponsors reside in Quebec we invite you to contact the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI).

## 1713 Validity of a temporary resident document with new 5903 No 2020-12-03 1

passport

Generally, immigration documents are issued according to the validity period of the applicant's passport. This means that the validity period of a temporary resident document, such as a work permit, study permit or visitor record, cannot exceed the passport expiry date.

Please note that the passport number indicated on your document has no impact on the information related to your current status. The passport number will only be updated once a new application to change conditions or extend your stay in Canada as a worker, student or visitor is submitted and a new document is issued.

### Useful info:

If you have an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) and obtain a new passport or if the

## information submitted when applying for your eTA

does not match the information that appears in your passport, please apply for a new eTA. To find out how long it may take to process your application, please visit the processing times page.

The health and safety of everyone is our priority. As we resume some of our in-person services, IRĆC has modified its approach in order to limit walk-in visits due to the coronavirus situation.

Whenever possible, interactions will occur virtually or through scheduled appointments only. Only clients with pre-scheduled appointments will be permitted into IRCC offices. Appointments letters will include specific instructions to prepare our clients for health and safety regulations.

Following federal, provincial and municipal public health guidelines remains a priority and an office may have to temporarily suspend in-person services based on these guidelines. If you had an in-person appointment scheduled at a local IRCC office which was cancelled, you will be contacted for the rescheduling of your appointment.

### 1778 Coronavirus-Public policy for temporary workers in 6002 No 2020-12-03 1

Canada

The Government of Canada is closely monitoring the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) and any impacts on IRCC clients.

A temporary public policy has come in effect for temporary workers already in Canada who are changing jobs or employers and have secured a new job offer. They can now get approval to start working in their new job, even while their work permit (WP) application is being fully processed.

To benefit from this public policy, a worker already in Canada must be:

A WP holder or a worker who can work without a WP, AND Have a valid Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or can be hired in an LMIA-exempt situation using the employer portal.

As always, open WP holders can change employers at any time.

To learn more about how to request consideration under the temporary public policy, please consult our website.

## 1822 6067

visitors to apply for a work permit without having to leave Canada

The Government of Canada is closely monitoring the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) and any impacts on IRCC clients.

To benefit employers in Canada who continue to face difficulties finding the workers they need, as well as temporary residents who would like to contribute to Canada's recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic, IRCC has put in place a public policy that will allow visitors to apply for a work permit without having to leave Canada.

### To be eligible, the applicant must:

Have valid status in Canada as a visitor on the day they apply, Have been in Canada on August 24, 2020 and

## remained in Canada,

Have a job offer, Submit an application for an employer-specific work permit that is supported by a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or an LMIA-exempt offer of employment, no later than March 31, 2021, and Meet all other standard admissibility criteria.

This temporary public policy also provides the opportunity for applicants who meet these criteria and who had a valid work permit in the past 12 months to begin working for their new employer before their work permit application has been fully approved. To do so, they need to follow these instructions.

For more information on the situation and to receive

### 1835Coronavirus-Changes to biometrics requirements -6083 No 2020-12-03 1

Permanent residence applicants

### The Government of Canada is closely monitoring

COVID-19 and any impacts on IRCC clients.

Until further notice, IRCC has put in place a public policy to exempt permanent residenice (PR) applicants who have previously given their

## biometrics in support of an application within the

last 10 years from having to give their biometrics as part of their application for PR.

You are exempt from giving biometrics if you have

### both of the following:

Already applied or are applying for PR within or outside Canada, and Given your biometrics in support of an immigration application (temporary or permanent residence or a claim) within the last 10 years.

The biometrics you have previously given will be reused for screening purposes during the processing of your PR application.

You do not have to pay the biometric fee when you submit your application, even if the system asks you to pay it.

If you paid the fee already, we

necessary income

We want to ensure to make the parents and grandparents sponsorship process as easy as possible by inviting you to read the following information concerning the minimum necessary income for 2020 for sponsors residing outside Quebec.

What is the minimum necessary income to sponsor your parents or your grandparents?

If you will submit the interest to sponsor form and then you're invited to apply, you must make sure that you meet the program requirements, including the income requirements. Your family size determines the minimum income to sponsor.

To know how to calculate your family size, we invite you to consult our website.

Given that many sponsors may have been financially impacted by the exceptional circumstances of the COVID-19 pandemic, IRCC is introducing a temporary public policy that will reduce the income requirement for the 2020 tax year to the minimum necessary income, instead of the minimum necessary income plus 30%.

For more details, we invite you to read the temporary public policy on our website.

### 1872Measures to support Hong Kong youth to come to 6126 No 2020-12-03 1

Canada

On November 12, 2020, IRCC announced a new immigration initiative that will attract students and youth from Hong Kong to Canada by offering a new open work permit and broadening their pathways to permanent residency.

More details on the new temporary and permanent pathways for Hong Kong youth and other facilitative measures are outlined in the backgrounder.

For information regarding priority processing, we invite you to consult our Help Centre.

News release available on our website.

# 1873Interim pathway for caregivers6127No 2020-12-03 1

The Interim Pathway for Caregivers was opened from July 8 to October 8, 2019. It is no longer possible to apply for permanent residence under this class. If you submitted an application on or before October 8, 2019, we'll continue to process it.

If you need to send us your language test results or educational credential assessment, follow the instructions in the guide.

If needed, more information is available for you regarding the interim pathway for caregivers.

COVID-19 and its impact on IRCC clients. Until further notice, most people cannot travel to Canada, even if they have a valid visitor visa or electronic travel authorization (eTA). You can travel to Canada, or be permitted to enter Canada, if you are an: Immediate family member of a Canadian citizen, person registered under Canada's Indian Act or permanent resident (PR). To be eligible, you must: make sure you meet the definition of immediate family member of a Canadian citizen, person registered under Canada's Indian Act or PR, andstay in Canada for 15 days or more, please follow these instructions. or Extended family member of a Canadian citizen, person registered under Canada's Indian Act or permanent resident (PR). To be eligible, you must: make sure you meet the definition of extended family member of a Canadian citizen, person registered under Canada's Indian Act or PR, stay in Canada for 15 days or more, and have written authorization from IRCC,please follow these instructions. If you are staying for less than 15 days, you must be travelling

## for an essential (non-discretionary) purpose. Furthermore, if you're travelling by air, you need to:

Pass a health check conducted by airlines before

### you'll be allowed to board your flight, and Wear a

non-medical mask or face covering during travel (including to the place you'll quarantine). "As of November 21, 2020, you must use ArriveCAN before checking in at the airport or crossing the border to

Please do not visit a Service Canada office to give your biometrics unless you have an appointment. If you miss your scheduled appointment for any reason, you can make a new appointment using the Service Canada Appointment System. We want to assure you that you do not have to give your biometrics until you are able to get an appointment. Your application will not be refused or closed if you cannot provide your biometrics within the deadline indicated on your BIL due to illness, quarantine or closures related to COVID-19. Here are some examples of circumstances that might warrant the issuance of the visa: When new, replacement or emergency passports cannot be issued in a sufficiently timely fashion and where the travel is urgent: for Canadians in distress (lost/stolen documents), for dual nationals coming to Canada for the first time, for dual nationals who did not obtain a Canadian passport prior to leaving Canada, Children born in Canada to foreign nationals, who have returned to their country, and do not wish to «claim» the citizenship automatically granted to Canadian born children, Foreign nationals who are adopted under the Citizenship adoption process, Etc. # Relay service calls (for people with hearing or speech disabilities)

Description Before Proceeding Procedure(s) Referrals Info-Client Further Info

## DESCRIPTION

001150

Immigration, RefugeesImmigration, Réfugiés and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

### A client contacts the Client Support Centre using a service for people

with hearing or speech disabilities such as, but not limited to: the Bell Relay Service; or the Video Relay Service (VRS). These are services that enable people with hearing or speech disabilities to communicate with voice telephone users. Professionally trained operators act as intermediaries to facilitate the call.

#### BEFORE PROCEEDING

When a client contacts the Client Support Centre using a service for people with hearing or speech disabilities it is your responsibility to take their call; Let the operator know at the beginning of the call if you are familiar

### with the service;

Listen carefully to the instructions provided by the operator.

NB: An operator calling for people with hearing or speech disabilities may obtain information on behalf of the client. See Training Modules for more information.

## PROCEDURE(S)

General tips that will help you better manage these calls:

Speak directly to the client (TTY user), not to the operator; Talk a bit more slowly than usual as the operator is typing in word for word what you are saying; Spell names; Always say "Go ahead" when you are finished; Always wait for the operator to say "Go ahead" before speaking.

## Questions Answers

What is the objective for the Client For 100% of calls to be coded.

#### Support Centre as far as coding calls is

concerned?

Will this affect my productivity? No, it is taken into account when assessing performance.

When are the best moments to enter During the call, while on hold, or at the end of the call the wrap-up code? (because the client will have asked all of their questions).

Some agents enter the code after the recapitulation; others look for the code while the client is on hold and enter the code once they are back with the client. You must find the best method for you, which brings the best

# INFO-CLIENT

Client Feedback Mechanism:

## General

FURTHER INFO If client is having technical problems filling out the form, follow this procedure.

## Q&A Q1: How long will it take to process my feedback?

We appreciate your feedback and what you think is important to us. We are not able to provide a personalized response to every message, but rest assured that we review and consider all comments. You are helping us understand what we do well, and what we need to focus on improving. Q2: What is the status of the feedback inquiry I sent? If you received a CFM reference number when you submitted your feedback, rest assured that it has been received and will be considered; however, please be advised that not all feedback receives a response. Example of the CFM confirmation number sent to clients: Thank you for submitting your feedback. Your feedback reference number is CFM 2019-50554 Example of the acknowledgement of receipt sent to clients: Thank you for contacting Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada. We appreciate this feedback about your service experience. What you think is important to us. We are not able to provide a personalized response to every message, but we review and consider all comments. You are helping us understand what we do well, and what we need to focus on improving.

001190

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

If you have questions about our programs and services, you can consult the online IRCC Help Centre.

Thank you,

## Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

Q3: How will my feedback information be used?

All feedback received will be read and considered as part of IRCC's continuous effort to improve service to our clients. It will not be used for any other purpose (such as making decisions on applications, etc.).

Q4: Will the feedback I sent have an impact on my status in Canada or the status of my application (or that of my family members)?

No, feedback is intended to improve our services and will not affect a person's immigration status or application to IRCC.

Q5: The subject/reason of my feedback is not in the drop down menu, what should I do?

Please select the closest option in the drop-down menu and describe your actual situation in the free text box using as much details as possible.

Q6: I changed my mind and want to cancel the feedback I sent. I do not wish for it to be processed, how do I do that?

The Client Feedback Mechanism web form does not allow withdrawing or modifying your submitted feedback.

Q7: I have submitted my feedback several days/weeks ago and have not yet received a response. Is there anything I can do to get a quicker response?

If you were shown a Client Feedback Mechanism confirmation number immediately following your submission (or afterwards by email, if an email address was provided), your feedback has indeed been received by IRCC. Submitting duplicate requests will not increase the likelihood or speed of a response.

We are not able to provide a personalized response to every message, but rest assured that we review and consider all comments. You are helping us understand what we do well, and what we need to focus on improving.

# Scripts

Important: Verify the CHD procedure and Info-Client texts, these may also help you to provide more details to clients.

Why don't you have more information available? I'm inside Canada. Can I go to a Port of Entry to receive immigration services? What will happen if I cannot travel to Canada before my Port of Entry letter expires? Appointments at a local IRCC office, have they started scheduling again? What can I do if I cannot get a LMIA or a SIN from Service Canada? Can I get an appointment to give my biometrics at a Service Canada office?/When will I receive a call from Service Canada? Processing times have passed. What is going on with my application?

### Why don't you have more information available?

"We recognize that the special measures established in response to the coronavirus (COVID-19), and at the Canadian borders may affect you (and your loved ones). We understand that this is a difficult time for you and are sorry for the difficulties you are facing due to these new measures.

001233

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

Rest assured that IRCC is working on giving you the most updated information as the situation evolves, and that all our efforts are dedicated to answering your concerns. Our website is updated regularly as more information is made available.

Given these circumstances, we invite you to continue visiting our website regularly to receive up-to- date information. To best serve you, we post new information as soon as it becomes available to us."

## I'm inside Canada. Can I go to a Port of Entry to receive immigration services?

"We recognize that the special measures established in response to the coronavirus (COVID-19), and at the Canadian borders may affect you (and your loved ones). We understand that this is a difficult time for you and are sorry for the difficulties you are facing due to these new measures.

Given the current situation, you should not travel to a Port of Entry to obtain immigration services. Travelling to a Port of Entry from inside Canada for the purpose of getting immigration services is not considered essential travel, and therefore immigration services are no longer provided to clients at the Port of Entry. This may change over time, but we don't know when.

We would like to invite you to continue visiting our website regularly to receive up-to-date information and instructions on how to apply for services. To best serve you, we post new information as soon as it becomes available to us."

## What will happen if I cannot travel to Canada before my Port of Entry letter

expires?

"We understand that this is a difficult time for you and are sorry for the difficulties you are facing due to these new measures.

If you are unable to travel to Canada before the expiration of your Port of Entry letter, please advise us by sending an IRCC Web form explaining your situation and why you are unable to travel.

Rest assured that our Department will be communicating with you as soon as possible to provide you with further instructions.

Given these circumstances, we invite you to continue visiting our website regularly to receive up-to- date information. To best serve you, we post new information as soon as it becomes available to us."

## Appointments at a local IRCC office, have they started scheduling again?

"We understand that this is a difficult time for you and are here to assist you by providing you the information we have available at this time.

001234

Immigration, Refugees 中 and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

IRCC started to resume some in-person services. Whenever possible, client interactions will occur virtually or through scheduled appointments only. Only clients with pre-scheduled appointments will be permitted into IRCC offices, and appointments letters will include specific instructions to prepare you for the new health and safety regulations.

## That being said, following federal, provincial and municipal public health guidelines remains a priority

and an office may have to temporarily suspend in-person services based on these guidelines.

Rest assured that you will be contacted with the next steps. Unfortunately, we cannot specify at this present moment when that will be.

In the meantime, we invite you to continue visiting our website regularly to receive up-to-date information. To best serve you, we post new information as soon as it becomes available to us."

What can I do if I cannot get a LMIA or a SIN from Service Canada?

"We understand that this is a difficult time for you and are sorry for the difficulties you are facing due to these new measures.

You can apply for a work permit only if you have a labour market impact assessment (LMIA) or if your employer has a LMIA application in process.

(If applicable) If you need a social insurance number, you must contact Service Canada to obtain one. May I suggest you consult their website to see how you can obtain one. IRCC does not issue social insurance numbers.

In the meantime, we invite you to continue visiting our website regularly to receive up-to-date information. To best serve you, we post new information as soon as it becomes available to us."

# Can I get an appointment to give my biometrics at a Service Canada

office?/When will I receive a call from Service Canada?

"Services are currently available by appointment only for permanent residence applicants who have received a Biometrics Instructions Letter (BIL) and have not given their biometrics within the last 10 years.

Service Canada officers have been contacting clients to schedule their biometrics appointment since mid-September. As of November 30, 2020, you can use the Service Canada Appointment System to schedule an appointment online.

Rest assured that your application will not be refused or closed if you cannot give your biometrics within the period indicated on your BIL due to COVID-19 service disruptions.

001235

Immigration, RefugeesImmigration, Réfugiés and Cizenship Canedaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

In the meantime, we invite you to continue visiting the IRCC and Service Canada websites regularly to obtain up-to-date information. To best serve you, we post new information as soon as it becomes available."

Processing times have passed. What is going on with my application?

We understand that this is a difficult time for you (or your loved ones) and we are here to assist you by providing you with the information we have available at this time.

Due to the current situation, IRCC offices are currently operating with reduced or critical staff only.

We are working on processing applications as quickly as possible; however, processing times are affected and disruptions caused by the novel coronavirus are not reflected accurately on our website. We aren't able to provide an estimate of the processing times; however, rest assured that we will make all the necessary efforts to finalize your application as soon as possible.

(If applicable) Since you have applied for TR extension before the expiry date of your current status,

### you can remain in Canada until a decision is made (implied status).

The office will communicate with you as soon as a decision is taken or if further information is necessary."

Reasons why IRCC decided to no longer send application forms and kits by mail

"Since December 1, 2011, IRCC is no longer printing and mailing out application forms and kits in an effort to:

Ensure applicants have the most recent forms available; Save costs to better serve clients; and Reduce our impact on the environment.

However, you have other great options such as downloading application kits directly from the IRCC website or applying online (for certain types of applications). Furthermore, our website will also give you access to our Help Centre to get answers to your questions."

### FURTHER INFO

The refund will be issued to the person identified as the payer on the back of the Payment receipt form (IMM 5401) or e-Payment receipt.

If the refund is to be issued to someone else, client must send a letter to the concerned CPC indicating the name and address of that person.

A refund cheque can be mailed to an address outside Canada; however, it is strongly recommended that the client provides an address in Canada (i.e., a friend or family member's address).

Overpayment and Refund Types and Payment of Fees Refunds

### Refunds issued by all offices:

Payments may be refunded:

Directly to the payer's credit/prepaid card, if the card details match the original payment; or If the credit/prepaid card details do not match, FIN Refunds will issue a cheque in the name of the payer: for CPC-M/CIO, the cheque will be issued in the name of the sponsor, regardless of the name of the payer. If the payment was made using a prepaid credit card, the client must keep that card for at least 18 months after the payment in case a

001310

Immigration, Refugees and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur laccès à Finformation

refund is required. If we can't refund the payment to the credit card, we will issue a cheque.

##### Additional information for CPC-M only:

When a refund is requested, CPC-M will send two letters to the client:

The first one confirms that a refund will be given to the client. The second one is sent within 4 weeks of the first one and confirms that the refund has been initiated. The refund is therefore initiated on the day that this second letter is sent to the client (also called a refund confirmation letter):

- in GCMS, in the IMM>Fees view, the status Refund Request will appear once the refund is initiated; and the status Refund Complete will appear once the refund is given to the client.
What is an undertaking and indemnity form?

It is a form sent to a client who has not received or lost a refund cheque. By completing and signing this form, the client solemnly declares not being in possession or having cashed the cheque. FIN Refunds will verify, and if applicable, a new cheque will be issued to the client.
