If the refund is to be issued to someone else, client must send a letter to the concerned CPC indicating the name and address of that person.

A refund cheque can be mailed to an address outside Canada; however, it is strongly recommended that the client provides an address in Canada (i.e., a friend or family member's address).

## Refunds issued by all offices:

Payments may be refunded:

Directly to the payer's credit/prepaid card, if the card details match the original payment; or If the credit/prepaid card details do not match, FIN Refunds will issue a cheque in the name of the payer: •for CPC-M/CIO, the cheque will be issued in the name of the sponsor, regardless of the name of the payer. If the payment was made using a prepaid credit card, the client must keep that card for at least 18 months after the payment in case a refund is required. If we can't refund the payment to the credit card, we will issue a cheque.

## Additional information for CPC-M only:

When a refund is requested, CPC-M will send two letters to the client:

The first one confirms that a refund will be given to the client. The second one is sent within four weeks of the first one and confirms that the refund has been initiated. The refund is therefore initiated on the day that this second letter is sent to the client (also called a "refund confirmation letter"):

- in GCMS, in the IMM>Fees view, the status Refund Request will appear once the refund is initiated, and the status Refund Complete will appear once the refund is given to the client.

"I see you attended your citizenship exam on XX and I would like to congratulate you, as you have passed the exam! This puts you on track for the next step, which may be an interview or the ceremony. As the current processing time for citizenship application is XX months, you may give us a call back if you have not received anything pass that time."

## Exam failed

"I see you attended your citizenship exam on XX and I regret to see that you did not pass your (first /second) exam:

1st fail (on or after June 3, 2013): When this occurs, rest assured that the office will take the time to reschedule you to retake the exam. This type of situation is not uncommon and the local office will contact you in writing with more information on how the process for retake works." 2nd fail: Even if this is your 2nd time not passing the exam, rest assured that we still have a process in place to help you move forward. When this occurs, the next step in the process is a hearing with a citizenship judge. You will be contacted in writing with more information on the hearing and the final decision on your application will be made by the citizenship judge following your hearing. I suggest you wait for the processing times to pass and if you have not received anything, you may call us back."

17.
# File Status

### Returned Incomplete Applications

## Scripts

Why is IRCC returning applications? Does this help improve processing times? (April 3, 2017, language evidence) The language evidence submitted was not on the list of acceptable evidence, what can I do? Will a returned application keep its place in the processing queue? What happens when an application is returned as incomplete? Urgent Cases-Identified My application was initially received before January 11, 2018, but it was returned. Which form versions do I need to send?

#### Why is IRCC returning applications?

"During a pilot project, IRCC assessed the operational impacts of retaining incomplete applications. During this exercise, mailroom staff checked all applications upfront for completeness, and then sent a letter to clients listing what elements of their application were incomplete and requesting these documents be sent to the Case Processing Centre. This process allowed to review a greater volume of complete applications that were ready for processing.

This process permits IRCC staff to devote much more time to processing complete applications, and allows to assess a higher rate of completed applications that are ready for processing, which reduces the processing times in the long run."

#### Does this help improve processing times?

### "Given the volume of incomplete applications received, the decision to return them makes processing

more efficient. It allows to focus on those applications that are complete upon receipt. It also allows the office to communicate with clients quickly to advise them of what is missing from the application, rather than having them wait months, in some cases, to be advised."

Immigration, Réfugiés Immigration, Refugees 中 et Citoyenneté Canada

## and Cizenship Canada

Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

## 001442

# April 3, 2017, language evidence-The language evidence submitted was not

# on the list of acceptable evidence, what can I do?

"If your application was returned because the language evidence submitted was not on the list of acceptable evidence, we invite you to resubmit your application for reconsideration. Please resubmit the same language evidence and include a note on the front of the application indicating Resubmission for reconsideration of language evidence.

Please note that if your application was returned because the language evidence was missing, illegible or demonstrated a level below CLB4, it will still be returned as incomplete."

## If an incomplete application is returned, does it keep its place in the queue for

# processing, according to the original date it was sent?

"IRCC considers an application to be received for processing only when it is complete. To determine the application processing time (according to the times posted on the IRCC website), you should use the date that you submit a complete application."

### Français Il Back to top

What happens when an application is returned as incomplete?

"Because the Case Processing Centre no longer keeps incomplete applications, I recommend you read the letter that was sent with the returned application. It indicates the missing documentation and offers you 2 options:

1. You may either resubmit the application with the missing information/documents; or
2. You may request the refund of fees because you no longer wish to submit your application.
The refund process is not automatic. If you no longer wish to submit the application, please return the notice letter indicating that you wish to get a refund.

If you choose to resubmit the application, please note that it is not necessary to re-sign or re-date the application, unless it is dated more than 90 days before we receive it (stale dated).

Also note that your physical presence will be calculated based on the date you signed your application and not on the date we received it."

### Urgent Cases-Identified

001443

"If you wrote Urgent on your envelope and included the proof of travel, the CPC will not return your application, but will contact you to obtain the missing information or document."

My application was initially received before January 31, 2019, but it was returned. Which form versions do I need to send?

"IRCC will continue to accept applications submitted with forms from October 2017 or later.

This also applies to applications originally received at the CPC before January 31, 2019, and returned as incomplete. Therefore, you will not be required to resubmit a new form version.

Nevertheless, you are required to submit any missing information or documents the CPC requests."

SCRIPT(S):

Will an incomplete application returned keep its place in the queue for processing, according to the original date it was sent?

"IRCC considers an application to be received for processing only when it is complete. To determine the application processing time, you should use the date when CPC-PRC Sydney begins to process the complete application."

001491

Immigration, Refugees and Cizenship Canedaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

What happens when an application is returned as incomplete?

"Because the Case Processing Centre no longer keeps incomplete applications, I recommend you read the notice letter that was sent back with the application. It indicates the missing documentation and offers you 2 options:

1. You may either resubmit the application with the missing information/documents; or
2. You may request a refund of the fees because you no longer wish to submit your application.
It is preferable to note that the refund process is not automatic. If you no longer wish to submit the application, please return the notice letter indicating that you wish to get a refund."

### Urgent cases-Identified

"If you wrote urgent on your envelope and included proof of travel because you are travelling in 30 days or less, CPC-PRC Sydney will not return your application. Instead, they will contact you for the missing information or documents.

However, if you are travelling in more than 30 days and the application is incomplete, it will be returned to you. You will need to include the missing information or documents and send it back to CPC-PRC Sydney. Please make sure you have written urgent on the envelope and included proof of travel."

The refund will be issued to the person identified as the payer on the back of the IPRMS receipt or on the online payment receipt.

If the refund is to be issued to someone else, client must send a letter to the PRC Sydney courier address indicating the name and address of that person.

Online payments may be refunded directly to the payer's credit card if the card details match the original payment and the card is still valid. If this is not the case, a refund cheque will be issued.

DESCRIPTION

Client contacted the Client Support Centre by webform using inappropriate language or behaviour.

## BEFORE PROCEEDING

The client is considered abusive if their enquiry contains:

Expression of racist, hateful, sexist, homophobic, slanderous, insulting messages; Aggressive, coarse, violent, obscene, or pornographic content; Offensive, rude, or abusive behaviour* to an individual or an organization.

As per IRCC's guidelines, you should not engage with a client demonstrating the above.

001536

Appointments may be cancelled to adhere to new restrictions put in place by local and regional health authorities. When it happens: clients are informed of the cancellation via telephone/email; and another appointment will be automatically rescheduled later on; Some VACs have temporarily closed or are operating with limited hours and services; The VAC Contact Centre is open; Citizenship and immigration applications will not be refused for non-compliance, and all

Determine the client's enquiry and identify their needs.

Ensure you fill out the Contacts related to Coronavirus tracker for sensitive cases only. Sensitive cases are exceptional scenarios where IRCC should consider taking action for a client, such as:

Clients who are unable to return to Canada and need to come back urgently; Clients in vulnerable circumstances (e.g., minors, clients with health issues, etc.); Situations that are not covered by the Program Delivery Instructions or where the procedures are problematic; Enquiries related to essential services in Canada (e.g., key work functions such as healthcare, supply chain, etc.);

# Procedures Situation in Lebanon-Tragedy in Beirut (for ESU dedicated email

agents only)

Client contacts us via the dedicated email address for the situation in Lebanon (IRCC.SituationLebanon-SituationLiban.IRCC@cic.gc.ca), and they inform us that they are affected by the explosion in Beirut, on Aug. 4, 2020, and they:

Want general information on: Canada's response to the crisis in Lebanon;

- the facilitative measures in place (eligibility, type of applications, documents to provide, etc.);
- what to do if they are in Lebanon and unsure if they are still a Canadian permanent resident;
- help for Canadian citizens; etc.;
Enquire on the fees and refunds; or Have already submitted an application and they are:

- in Lebanon and wish to come to Canada; or
- a Lebanese citizen in Canada on a temporary basis.
#### BEFORE PROCEEDING

Important:

To be eligible under the facilitative measures, effective from Sept. 2, 2020, to Jan. 31, 2021, client must be a: 0Canadian citizen in Lebanon who urgently needs a Canadian passport, temporary passport, emergency travel document and/or citizenship certificate (proof) to urgently return to Canada; Canadian permanent resident (PR) in Lebanon who urgently needs a permanent resident travel document (PRTD) to travel to Canada; 0Lebanese citizen personally affected by the explosion in Beirut and who is an immediate family member of a Canadian citizen or Canadian PR and urgently needs a temporary resident visa (TRV) to join their loved ones in Canada; or 0Lebanese citizen whose temporary residence (TR) status in Canada will soon or recently expired and they are unable to return in Lebanon due to the explosion; An exemption to the travel restrictions allows immediate family members of Canadian

### citizens and PRs to enter Canada to visit if they:

do not show signs of COVID-19;

stay for at least 15 days; Oare admissible; and Otravel with a valid travel document and passport.

## Fees and refunds

Types of fees that will not be collected for applications submitted between Sept. 2, 2020, and Jan. 31, 2021:

Temporary Canadian passport (proof of travel to Canada required); Canadian passport valid for 1 year (proof of travel to Canada required); Adult and child emergency Canadian travel document (proof of travel to Canada required); Lost/stolen passport replacement fee; Replacement Canadian citizenship certificate (paper application); for an online application, see below; PRTD; and TR status extension/renewal.

Types of fees that will be collected for applications submitted between Sept. 2, 2020, and Jan. 31, 2021:

New Canadian citizenship certificate; Replacement Canadian citizenship certificate (online application); those fees will be refunded if client is eligible; TRV; Restoration of TR status; Fees charged by a Visa Application Centre (VAC).

If client paid the fees (e.g., they have applied online), they will be refunded automatically. Refunds will take some time as they will be processed and issued once normal operations resume.

## DESCRIPTION

A temporary resident (TR) in Canada enquires about the steps to follow in order to validate their Confirmation of permanent residence (CoPR) received from a visa office or CPC-O.

001655

Immigration, Refugees and Cizenship Canedaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

## BEFORE PROCEEDING

Pilot proiect to confirm selected permanent residents by telephone: This pilot project has ended. There are currently no known initiatives where clients are being confirmed their permanent residence by telephone. However, it is possible that this method is being used in remote areas.

If applicable, follow this procedure in order to update the client's contact information (and their family members in Canada who will be granted PR status). Duplicate UCIs may exist for these clients and/or other applicants in the file: IMPORTANT: If a household is required for another applicant, client must provide required identifiers for them. if client did not provide all identifiers for the requester, reply to client using the text Household required (family member) - Missing identifiers. if client provided all identifiers for the requester, follow this procedure.

- Verify if client satisfies the requirements (R71.1) to be granted PR status within Canada:
is a member of the Economic or Family class; and has a valid TR status in Canada (including implied status): if client did not provide information on their status and it cannot be found in GCMS, reply to client using the text Missing valid TR status information.

Determine if the person contacting us is the principal applicant (PA); if they are not the PA, verify that the latter is already a PR or will be granted PR status at the same time as them. If not, reply to family member with the text Principal applicant must be granted PR status first.

## FURTHER INFO

Originals of the following documents are required to be granted PR status:

Passport, travel or identity document (including secure visa counterfoil (IMM 1346), if applicable); CoPR (IMM 5292/5688) and instructions issued by the visa office or CPC-O; Proof of legal status in Canada, such as: a valid WP, SP, TRP, or VR; or proof of implied status. Client must provide as many documents as possible proving implied status (i.e., payment receipt, copy of their paper application, printout of their e-application, proof of mailing, etc.). The officer will evaluate the information provided on a case-by-case basis; Any WP, SP, TRP, or VR in their possession, whether valid or not. For a regulatory landing at IRCC Montreal, the client will have to present a CSQ or convince the officer that he will establish outside Quebec after the appointment. Failure to meet one or the other requirement may lead to refusal of landing.

enquiries specialists)

A student changed post-secondary schools and must inform IRCC; however, they are unable to transfer DLI using their online account.

#### BEFORE PROCEEDING

In order to transfer DLI, client must provide:

Their new school's DLI number; and The date they started studying at their new school (MM/YYYY);

- if client did not provide the required information, reply to them using the text Linking an application-Unable to transfer DLI-Missing information.
Exceptions:

If client is not providing the DLI number, but is providing their school's exact name and location, you can obtain the DLI number from the IRCC website. If client is providing a future start date, reply to client using the text DLI transfer-Future start date (for designated agents only).

41. Procedures > Email Support Unit > Evaluating a proof of travel for PRC-Urgent requests
## Information

# Evaluating a proof for PRC-Urgent requests

IMPORTANT:

It is not up to you to decide what is a serious illness or a valid proof of urgency. If the client provided all necessary information from Step 2, you can consider that the request is complete. PRC-S will verify the documents provided before issuing the PR Card.

### For exceptions or grey areas, you should still forward the proof to PRC-S for assessment.

# Step 1:

In order to qualify for urgent processing of a PR Card, the client must demonstrate that they require their PR Card to travel within the next three months, and that they are leaving in more than 3 weeks, for the following reasons:

Own serious illness; Serious illness or death of a family member; To obtain employment; or Due to employment requirements or opportunity.

### Step 2:

The following documents (in English or French) must be included in the request:

- The proof of travel*, such as a ticket or an itinerary, must show: the client's personal information; the dates they will be traveling; and
- their destination;
- The proof of payment must show that the ticket is paid in full as well as:
- the date they paid;
001834

Immigration, Refugees 串 and Cizenship Canedaot Cioyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

- the full amount paid; and how they paid (e.g., cash, cheque (chq, chk), credit card (cc, ext), debit card, etc.);
A letter of explanation indicating the reason for the urgency (an

## explanation included in the body of an email is admissible);

Proof of the urgency (e.g., doctor's note, death certificate, letter from employer, etc.).

*For examples of fraudulent proof of travel, please see under: G:\CSU\CRU_Proof of Travel Examples.

## Description of the Web response quality assessment form-Positive

# client experience approach

This document is addressed to all Email Support Unit (CSU) agents at the IRCC Client Support Centre.

It provides you with a detailed description of the assessment form sections and contains tips, tricks and reminders for the different parts of a successful email.

To attain a positive client experience, there are three main elements that need to be achieved:

Providing accurate, correct information that answers the client's needs; Offering a service that is courteous, polite, and respectful by

### following the email etiquette;

Using an approach that is focused on reassuring the client while

### maintaining a positive approach throughout the email.

Section D : Email completion Definition of a quality web response

### Section C: Client service delivery excellence

# Definition of a quality web response

The client's needs are met in one email because the CSU agent has applied the roles and responsibilities of the IRCC Client Support Centre Mandate (page to come) and has demonstrated efficiency and effectiveness through the use of:

# A clear email structure (e.g., CSC Muscle tool); Client service excellence (e.g., proper communication skills);

Reassurance throughout the email while maintaining a positive approach; Appropriate tools (e.g., Info-Client, GCMS, internal updates, CHD procedures, Connexion etc.); and Initiative and accountability when working with clients to resolve issues.

By using the above, the client's needs should be met in one email exchange and the Client Support Centre's mission will then be accomplished!

# Quality assessment breakdown

Please note that emails are evaluated section by section, rather than based on the overall email.

The assessment ratings for the respective sections are broken down as follows:

001836

Immigration, Refugees 中 and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

Succeeded: The agent accomplished all the necessary items in the section while remaining polite and reassuring towards the client. Succeeded - : The agent missed or overlooked one item in the section that had little or no impact on the client or on IRCC. Did Not Meet: The agent missed or overlooked: several items in the section with little or no impact on the client or on IRCC, or

- missed or overlooked one (or more) items that had a direct impact on the client or on IRCC.
# SECTION A: Needs assessment

The Needs assessment section contains two categories:

Comprehensive reading Questioning skills

To understand the overall results of this section, please refer to the Quality assessment breakdown section above.

Below you will find the description for each item, as well as tips and tricks on how to be successful in this section.

### Comprehensive reading

For a successful needs assessment, comprehensive reading is to be used in order to fully understand what the client is contacting IRCC for. Comprehensive reading allows you to fully assess and understand the client's needs. It also helps you avoid answering too quickly and missing key pieces of information in the email you are reading.

When reading an email query, you must:

Put yourself in the client's situation/position. Analyze the client's question versus their actual need. Gather and analyze as much information as possible to fully assess and understand the email request. Adapt to their communication style.

## Questioning skills

Questioning avoids assuming what the client wants and helps ensure that the client's expectations are understood. If the client's request is unclear or insufficient information has been provided, you must use proper questioning to clarify the situation and gain a full understanding and analysis of the situation.

In order to avoid the need for unnecessary additional email exchanges with the client, it is best to be proactive and conduct preliminary research in client's files, data systems and procedures. This will help anticipate actions to be taken later on (such as referrals) and allow agents to request additional information accordingly. The use of closed/specific questioning is very important when determining the reason for the email and/or to determine the nature of an issue. (e.g., asking for a specific screen shot to determine if the client's issue is caused by a technical problem or simply by the user).

Presentation/Delivery

Once the client's needs have been clearly established, and you have found the appropriate solution using your tools, the information should be presented in a gradual, affirmative, logical, and methodical manner so that it can be easily understood.

Helpful tips on how to structure your answer:

Answer each of the client's questions directly with clear, impartial and honest answers; Provide the information in a sequential manner;

001844

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

Use an approach that is reassuring/positive and ensure to have empathy (if the situation merits this). Please see Section C-Positivity/Reassurance/Empathy, for more information.

Guidelines:

Be concise: Answer each of the client's questions and provide clear, precise, impartial explanations. Use simple expressions and avoid repetitions. Use short sentences: Focus on essential points related to the situation and avoid lengthy explanations. Use positive words of action and accountability: When a client expresses their concern, reassure them by explaining the steps you have taken to address the situation (e.g., We have sent a message to the Case Processing Centre to advise them that you have changed your address and requesting that the correspondence be resent.). Provide complete and relevant answers: Answer all of the client's questions to avoid unnecessary further email exchanges and ensure complete agent satisfaction. Read the email before you send it.

Some things can lead to an inefficient delivery:

When a logical sequence is not followed. Focusing on points that are irrelevant and that in no way would be beneficial to the client's situation or the progress/development of the email.

# Language

Your awareness of email risks and etiquette will protect IRCC from liability, complaints and potentially costly lawsuits. Agents are responsible for upholding IRCC's image at all times, by ensuring that the content of their emails is in line with the IRCC Code of Conduct, and thus delivered in a professional, impartial and ethical way.

By using proper language, IRCC will convey a professional image.

It is important to respect the client's language choice of the official language they used to communicate with IRCC. For example, if a client chose an English webform title but wrote their question in French, you must reply in French.

Below are certain key points for you to remember:

Use proper spelling, grammar, syntax and punctuation;

## Use an active instead of a passive tense;

Keep your language gender neutral; Personalize your email response; Do not use internal jargon; Make use of transition words to connect one paragraph to the next when providing multiple responses in the same email (e.g., Furthermore, In addition, Lastly, etc.).

### Verify if client:

Received their letter of introduction and wants to validate their document as they are already in Canada; Forgot to show their letter of introduction at the POE upon entry; Was advised that their immigration document could not be validated: pilot projects at some POEs may affect clients when they choose to leave and re-enter Canada at a land border, especially during the peak periods such as weekends; or Could not have it printed due to a technical problem at the POE.

How to validate Important: Until further notice, do not offer these two options to the client. document See the applicable section in the Coronavirus procedure.

Caller is a child who reveals they are a victim of abuse:

"I'm sorry to hear this happened to you. Canada takes violence seriously and your safety is of highest priority. I understand this must be difficult. This is not your fault. You did the right thing by telling me. I believe you and I will try to help. Is there someone that you trust that could help you? If you need help, call the police by dialing 911.

If you allow me to ask you some questions related to the events that took place, I will refer the information you provided to the responsible IRCC office for their action.

In order to gather key information, could you please describe the situation and how the person has treated you?"

Caller discloses they have abused a child:

"I'm sorry to hear this happened. If you need help (as a parent), you can contact the responsible provincial and territorial child protection authorities.

In order to gather key information, could you please describe the situation?"

### Required Documents

Originals of the following documents are required to be granted PR status:

Passport, travel or identity document (including secure visa counterfoil (IMM 1346), if applicable); CoPR (IMM 5688) and instructions issued by the visa office or CPC; Proof of legal status in Canada, such as: a valid WP, SP, TRP, or VR; or

# proof of implied status. Client must provide as many

documents as possible proving implied status (i.e., payment receipt, copy of their paper application, printout of their e-application, proof of mailing, etc.). The officer will evaluate the information provided on a case-by-case basis; Any WP, SP, TRP, or VR in their possession, whether valid or not; For a regulatory landing at IRCC Montreal, the client will have to present a CSQ or convince the officer that he will establish outside Quebec after the appointment. Failure to meet one or the other requirement may lead to refusal of landing.

### DESCRIPTION

OR

002028

if refugee claim was abandoned or withdrawn (see App Status Reason field in GCMS) and client claims that it was subsequently re-opened by IRB, they should be eligible for IFHP coverage; (if applicable) the expiry date of the IFHP coverage in GCMS;

and if an application was sent.

Important:

- A new IFH certificate of eligibility (plain paper, no photo) is sent to the client. The effective date can be either:
in the past, if coverage needs to be backdated; or in the future, not more than four months from the date coverage is created, so that coverage can be extended without overlaps (i.e., one day after the current coverage expires). For example, a client whose IFHP coverage expires on January 29, 2014, may apply for and be granted an extension of that coverage on January 5, 2014, with an effective date of January 30, 2014. All IFHP coverage issued after April 1, 2016, do not have an expiry date;

- for more details, please see Validity of the Coverage section of the training module; if the client had an active IFHP coverage as of April 1, 2016, they do not need to re-apply as coverage was automatically extended in GCMS.

### FURTHER INFO

### Important:

This procedure applies if:

## notes on file indicate "LMIA XX in progress/pending";

however, it is still mandatory to verify the status of the LMIA in the system; client is applying for restoration of status; however, the

### application will be refused if the LMIA is still not approved when processing begins.

### If client applies for a LMIA and resides in the province of Quebec,

ESDC will contact the MIFI and the CAQ will be processed concurrently. If client's CAQ expired earlier than their LMIA (i.e. Live-in caregiver) they may apply for their CAQ directly through the MIFI.

### When an employer submits an LMIA application for multiple

employees, ESDC processes it as a "no named worker". Once the LMIA is validated, the employer must submit the names of workers they want to hire and then the system is updated with names. The WP application will be refused if the client's name does not appear in the system when the WP process begins.

### Mailing Date (paper application)

The CPC will substract up to 7 calendar days from the received date to determine the mailing date when assessing if an application was sent within 2 weeks from the expiry of status.

#### BEFORE PROCEEDING

Determine if the client is seeking new or secondary employment, or wants to stay with the same employer; In the case of a legal strike, clients have several means of recourse, including: waiting out the strike with minimal strike pay (like others in the same situation); finding another position and proceeding with the normal WP application process; or Oleave Canada.

# FURTHER INFO

What will CPC-E do after receiving an Extension Application in Strike Situations:

CPC-E will log receipt of the application and then place the application on hold for four months. The client will have implied status during this time. If the client provides a valid LMIA to CPC-E during the four-month period, CPC-E can finalize processing accordingly. CPC-E will not check for the presence of an LMIA within this period. Four months after receipt in CPC-E, the application will be finalized by CPC-E, whether the strike is over or not. If the LMIA is still outstanding, CPC-E will contact the client to request the LMIA, allowing 30 calendar days for reply. CPC-E will finalize processing once the outstanding LMIA is received, or after 30 days if no reply is received.

Foreign workers: Assessing in the event of a strike situation

### BEFORE PROCEEDING

Applicants* must meets the minimum requirements to apply for a transportation loan: •they must provide evidence that they are unable to pay the transportation costs and that they cannot obtain a loan from other sources; they must prove that they are able to repay the loan within the time limits prescribed by the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; they must prove that the visas have been issued and that the people subject to the loan are able to travel; the people who are the subject of the transportation loan must be outside Canada; Processing times are available on applicable local offices Info pages.

*A transportation loan applicant may be a foreign national applying for permanent residence under any category or a Convention refugee or person in need of protection and their dependents. In addition, Canadian citizens and permanent residents may apply for a loan on behalf of a dependent.

## English

We verified the information on your file. In order to meet the criteria under the Federal Skilled Work program, you must have the required work experience under your Primary Occupation NOC. Primary Occupation' is the job you have experience in, and that we will use to assess if you meet the minimum requirements for programs under Express Entry.

Note: Your primary occupation may not be your most recent work experience. It is the job you have the required experience in, and want to base your application on. If you do not

have the minimum work experience in the primary occupation National Occupational Classification (NOC) that you choose, you may be ineligible.

## Issue: eTa applicants with US Green Cards without expiry dates.

Dute entered: 17-July-2017 Background: US lawful permanent residents are eligible to apply for an eTA. When doing so, they need to provide their US green card number, as well as that card's expiry date. The expiry date is a mandatory field. Since some cards do not have expiry dates, clients can't complete the application process.

Workaround: Agents who receive these enquiries should reply with the following text:

## English

Thank you for your email regarding your application for an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA). We are sorry to hear you are experiencing issues applying for an eTA using your

U.S. Green Card that has no expiry date. To be able to submit your eTA application, all data entry fields on the application form must be completed – this includes the date of expiry for your U.S. Green Card. For the date of expiry field on the form, select the same date of expiry as noted on your passport in the drop-down menu. Once all the fields are completed, you should be able to submit your form. If you encounter any other issues, please contact us via our secureweb form. Be sure to select 'Electronic Travel Authorization' and ‘General and Technical Enquiries' from the first two drop-down menus.

STUDENTS APPLYING FOR PGWP WITH EXPIRED STATUS WITHIN 9O-DAYS

Issue: Students have up to 180 days to apply for a PGWP after completing their course but their SP may have expired. Background: Students who want to apply for their PGWP with an expired SP (within restoration period) may apply online as per our website. In order to complete the process correctly, applicants must apply online for the PGWP and pay the correct fee ($255), and pay the fee to restore status as a student ($350) 0Due to system limitations, applicants must pay the fees to restore their status as a student online and attach a copy of the receipt to their PGWP online application. Applicants do not need to make a separate application to restore their status as a student. They can't work until their study permit and work permit have been approved. If they don't apply within the 90 days, or if the 90 days have already passed, they must leave Canada.
